definition_zh: 奶奶；外婆；婆婆；老大娘
definition_en: an informal word for a grandmother, or an elderly woman in general
core_image: 门口藤椅上的老奶奶：叫一声就会应的家人称呼
scene: 孩子们放学跑进院子，老远就喊了起来。 Granny waved from under the apple tree.
sceneCN: 这里 granny 是「奶奶、外婆」（第 1 个义项：祖母的亲昵叫法）；句意为奶奶在苹果树下挥手。

pos.zh: 名词：奶奶；外婆（口语亲昵称呼）

青苹果品种（澳洲老妇名字）

另一亲昵简称

senses.title: An affectionate word for grandmother
senses.definition: an informal, loving name for a grandmother
senses.definitionCN: 对祖母的非正式爱称
senses.example: Granny baked cookies with us on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶周日和我们一起烤饼干。
senses.why: The core image is a child's own name for the family elder.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是孩子自己给家中长者起的名字。

senses.title: Any elderly woman
senses.definition: an informal word for any old woman
senses.definitionCN: 泛指任何年长女性的口语说法
senses.example: A kind granny showed us the way.
senses.exampleCN: 一位热心老大娘给我们指了路。
senses.why: The family name opens its door to strangers of the same age.
senses.whyCN: 家人的称呼向同龄的陌生老人敞开了门。

senses.title: Old-fashioned or fussy style
senses.definition: a style seen as old-fashioned, like granny clothes
senses.definitionCN: 被视为过时的、像老人衣着的风格
senses.example: That granny sweater is back in fashion.
senses.exampleCN: 那种老奶奶毛衣又流行回来了。
senses.why: The person's name becomes the style itself.
senses.whyCN: 人的称呼变成了风格的名字。

intro.en: Granny is grandma grown one suffix longer.
intro.cn: granny 是 grandma 再长一个词尾的变体。

items.en: Latin grandis meant large or grown.
items.cn: 拉丁语 grandis 意为大、成年。

items.en: Old French grand fed the English kinship prefix.
items.cn: 古法语 grand 供养了英语亲属前缀。

items.en: Grandame was an older pet form for an old woman.
items.cn: 中古英语 grandame 是更早的年长女性爱称。

items.en: Granny formed as a nursery variant with the -y ending.
items.cn: 现代英语中 granny 以 -y 词尾构成儿语式变体。

items.en: The style sense later grew in fashion talk.
items.cn: 现代英语后来在时尚语境中长出风格义。

note.en: Granny, grandma and grandmother climb from informal to formal.
note.cn: granny、grandma、grandmother 由口语到正式层层排列。

entries.definition: more than one granny
entries.definitionCN: granny 的复数

entries.definition: the bare prefix word meaning splendid
entries.definitionCN: 前缀本词：极好的、宏伟的

entries.definition: another affectionate short form
entries.definitionCN: 另一亲昵简称

entries.definition: a polite general phrase
entries.definitionCN: 礼貌的泛称说法

normalIntro.en: Five hooks to keep granny in the rocking chair.
normalIntro.cn: 五条钩子把 granny 安在藤椅上。

normal.en: Granny sounds babyish: children invented it.
normal.cn: granny 听起来像儿语：是孩子们叫出来的。

normal.en: A granny flat is a tiny house for granny.
normal.cn: granny flat 是给奶奶住的小屋。

normal.en: Granny Smith apples got a real granny's name.
normal.cn: 青苹果 Granny Smith 用了真老奶奶的名字。

normal.en: Granny knots come loose: old hands tied them fast but loose.
normal.cn: granny knot 容易松：外行结不牢。

normal.en: Two n's and a y make granny easy to spell.
normal.cn: 两个 n 加一个 y，granny 拼写不难。

abstract.en: Granny is the name said loudest from the gate.
abstract.cn: granny 是在大门口喊得最响的那个名字。

abstract.en: Her shawl smells of tea and sun.
abstract.cn: 她的披肩有茶和阳光的味道。

abstract.en: Every granny was once somebody's little girl.
abstract.cn: 每个老奶奶都曾是谁家的小女孩。

examples.en: Granny tells better stories than television.
examples.cn: 奶奶讲的故事比电视还好看。

examples.en: The granny next door grows the best tomatoes.
examples.cn: 隔壁的老大娘种的番茄最好。

examples.en: He wore a granny cardigan to the party.
examples.cn: 他穿着老奶奶式的开衫去参加聚会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歌拉妮」——隔代的老母亲总被孩子拉着衣角喊；granny 就是被拉着喊的那位

sensesIntro.en: From the family nickname to any elder and her old-fashioned style.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从家人的昵称，扩展到泛称老妇与老派风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the elder called by her child-given name
core.cn: 核心意象：被孩子名字唤着的长者

branches.cn: 街上任何老大娘

branches.cn: 老派风格的标签

intro.cn: granny 展示了英语如何把正式词宠成儿语形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin grandis sits far upstream; granny is nursery speech.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 grandis 在很远的上游；granny 属儿语层。

definition_zh: 糟糕地；差劲地；严重地；非常；处境困难
definition_en: in a poor or wrong way, severely, or very much
core_image: 一块歪掉的画框被越推越斜
scene: 墙上的画框本来就歪了，他又伸手推了一下，斜得更厉害。 He hurt his knee badly when he fell off the bike.
sceneCN: 这里 badly 是「严重地」（第 2 个义项：程度很重）；句意为他从自行车上摔下来时膝盖伤得很重。

pos.zh: 副词：糟糕地；严重地；非常

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「坏的；有害的」
由 bad 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「坏；恶劣」
bad 的比较级，义为「更坏的」
bad 的最高级，义为「最坏的」

senses.title: In a poor way
senses.definition: in a way that is not good or not skillful
senses.definitionCN: 以不好或不熟练的方式
senses.example: She sings badly, but she never gives up.
senses.exampleCN: 她唱得不好，但从不放弃。
senses.why: Bad names what is not good, and the suffix -ly turns it into the manner of doing something, so doing a thing in a bad way is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: bad 指「不好」，后缀 -ly 把它变成做事情的方式，所以「以不好的方式做事」是最先长出的义项。

senses.title: Severely
senses.definition: to a serious or severe degree
senses.definitionCN: 达到严重或厉害的程度
senses.example: He cut his hand badly while cooking.
senses.exampleCN: 他做饭时把手割得很重。
senses.why: If an action goes in a bad direction, it can go far in that direction, and this gives the sense of severe degree.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事朝坏的方向发展，就可能坏得很深，于是有了「程度严重」这个义项。

senses.title: Very much
senses.definition: very much, especially with need or want
senses.definitionCN: 非常，尤用于需要或想要
senses.example: I badly need a good sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 我非常需要好好睡一觉。
senses.why: Something that is badly needed is needed in a strong, almost painful degree, so the word came to mean simply very much.
senses.whyCN: 急需的东西，需要的程度又强又急，几乎带着痛感，于是这个词也引申为「非常」。

senses.title: Without success
senses.definition: to perform poorly in an exam, match, or competition
senses.definitionCN: 在考试、比赛或竞争中表现很差
senses.example: Our team did badly in the first half.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队上半场打得很差。
senses.why: Here the bad manner is measured by a result: the performance itself is the thing that turns out badly.
senses.whyCN: 这里「坏的方式」用结果来衡量：表现本身就是那个变坏的东西。

senses.title: In a bad position
senses.definition: in the phrase badly off, having very little money or few advantages
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 badly off，指钱很少或条件很差
senses.example: After the factory closed, many families were badly off.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关闭后，许多家庭生活困难。
senses.why: The bad manner is now applied to a whole situation, so a person's circumstances themselves are in a bad state.
senses.whyCN: 「坏的方式」这时落到整个处境上，于是人的境况本身处于糟糕状态。

intro.en: Badly is a plain English adverb built from the adjective bad and an old suffix; the deeper origin of bad itself is uncertain.
intro.cn: badly 是地道的英语副词，由形容词 bad 加古老后缀构成；bad 本身更早的来源不确定。

items.en: A form badde is recorded in Old English, but its deeper origin is uncertain and different explanations exist.
items.cn: 古英语中记录有 badde 这一形式，但它更早的来源不确定，存在不同解释。

items.en: The adjective bad becomes common in Middle English, and the sources still do not agree on where it came from.
items.cn: 形容词 bad 在中古英语中变得常见，各家对它从何而来仍未取得一致。

items.en: The adverb suffix -ly goes back to Old English -lice, meaning in the manner of.
items.cn: 副词后缀 -ly 可追溯到古英语 -lice，意为「以……的方式」。

items.en: The adverb badly is recorded in Middle English; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 副词 badly 在中古英语中已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense very much, as in badly needed, grows later beside the older sense of severe degree.
items.cn: 「非常」这一义项，如 badly needed 中的用法，是较晚在「程度严重」之外发展出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the bad family and the comparison forms; the near-meaning group gathers other adverbs that describe a poor or severe way.
note.cn: 形近组收 bad 这一词族与比较级形式；近义组收其他表示「差」或「严重」的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning not good, harmful, or serious.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「坏的、有害的、严重的」，是 badly 的基础词。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being bad.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「坏、恶劣」，由 bad 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: The comparative of bad, meaning more bad or more serious.
entries.definitionCN: bad 的比较级，义为「更坏的、更严重的」。

entries.definition: The superlative of bad, meaning the most bad.
entries.definitionCN: bad 的最高级，义为「最坏的」。

entries.definition: In a weak or unsatisfactory way; close to badly but more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「糟糕地、不佳地」，与 badly 接近但更正式。

entries.definition: In a very serious or harsh way; it matches the severe sense of badly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「严重地、严厉地」，对应 badly 的「严重」义项。

entries.definition: Very much; it matches the degree sense of badly without any bad meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「非常、大大地」，对应 badly 的程度义，但不带「坏」的色彩。

entries.definition: In a good or skillful way; the direct opposite of the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「好、很好地」，是第一个义项的直接反义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real pieces of the word: the adjective bad, the suffix -ly, and the irregular comparison worse and worst.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个词的真实构件：形容词 bad、后缀 -ly，以及不规则的比较级 worse 与最高级 worst。

normal.en: Bad plus -ly simply means in a bad way, just as quick plus -ly gives quickly.
normal.cn: bad 加 -ly 就是「以坏的方式」，正如 quick 加 -ly 成为 quickly。

normal.en: The comparison is irregular: bad, worse, worst, and badly follows the same pattern.
normal.cn: 比较级不规则：bad、worse、worst，badly 也沿用这一套。

normal.en: Badly hurt and badly damaged both show the sense of severe degree.
normal.cn: badly hurt 与 badly damaged 都体现「程度严重」这个义项。

normal.en: Badly needed means needed very much, not needed in a bad way.
normal.cn: badly needed 意为「非常需要」，不是「以坏的方式需要」。

normal.en: Badly off describes a person whose situation is poor, not an action done poorly.
normal.cn: badly off 描述的是人的境况差，而不是动作做得差。

abstract.en: Picture a crooked frame on the wall: every push makes it more crooked, and that is the direction the word points.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一只歪画框：每推一下都更歪，这个词指的就是这个方向。

abstract.en: A badly tied knot comes apart, a badly hurt knee cannot bend, and the same word covers both.
abstract.cn: 系得很糟的结会散开，伤得很重的膝盖弯不了，同一个词把两件事都盖住了。

abstract.en: The word does not add a new idea; it only pushes the idea of bad into the verb or the situation.
abstract.cn: 这个词不增加新意思，只是把「坏」推进动作或处境里去。

examples.en: He hurt his knee badly when he fell off the bike.
examples.cn: 他从自行车上摔下来时膝盖伤得很重。

examples.en: The team played badly in the rain and lost the game.
examples.cn: 球队在雨中打得很差，输掉了比赛。

examples.en: I badly need a glass of water after the long run.
examples.cn: 长跑之后我非常需要一杯水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「掰得离」——一掰就坏，只好离远点：糟糕地、严重地

root: 由形容词 bad「坏的」加副词后缀 -ly 构成；-ly 来自古英语 -lice，意为「以……的方式」。bad 在古英语中已有 badde 形式，但更早词源存疑，各说不一。比较级 worse 与最高级 worst 为不规则形式。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of badly all push the idea of bad outward: into the manner of an action, the severity of damage, the strength of a need, the result of a performance, and the state of a whole situation.
sensesIntro.cn: badly 的五个义项都把「坏」向外推：推进动作的方式、伤害的程度、需要的强度、表现的结果，以及整个处境的状况。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a picture frame hangs crooked, and every touch pushes it further out of line.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上的画框本就歪着，每碰一下都更偏离原位。

branches.en: THE MANNER: an action is done in a bad way, so the adverb first describes how.
branches.cn: 方式线：动作以坏的方式进行，所以副词最先描述「怎么做」。

branches.en: THE SEVERITY: the bad direction goes deep, and the word measures how serious the damage is.
branches.cn: 程度线：坏的方向走得很深，这个词就用来衡量伤害有多重。

branches.en: THE STRENGTH: a need felt this strongly becomes simply a very great need.
branches.cn: 强度线：被感受到如此强烈的需要，就变成了「非常」的需要。

branches.en: THE RESULT: when the manner is judged by an outcome, doing badly means failing to do well.
branches.cn: 结果线：当方式由结果来评判时，do badly 就是没能做好。

branches.en: THE SITUATION: the same bad state spreads from one action to a whole life, giving hardship.
branches.cn: 处境线：同样的坏状态从一个动作扩展到整个生活，就有了「生活困难」。

intro.en: Badly is a transparent English formation: a common adjective plus the adverb suffix -ly, with an irregular comparison.
intro.cn: badly 是结构透明的英语构词：常见形容词加副词后缀 -ly，比较级不规则。

latinIntro.en: Bad and its suffix belong to Germanic English; no Latin cognate is recorded, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: bad 及其后缀属于日耳曼语来源的英语，没有记录在案的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.example: The weather was bad all week.
It turns bad into badly and quick into quickly.
items.exampleCN: 它把 bad 变成 badly，把 quick 变成 quickly。
它由 bad 构成 badness。

items.example: The second test was worse than the first.
items.exampleCN: 第二次测验比第一次更糟。

items.example: That was the worst day of the trip.
items.exampleCN: 那是旅行中最糟的一天。

items.example: The family was badly off that winter.
items.exampleCN: 那年冬天这家人生活困难。

items.example: The village received badly needed medicine.
items.exampleCN: 村子收到了急需的药品。

definition_zh: 到；向；往；向……（表示方向）；给；对于；（不定式标记）
definition_en: a preposition of direction, destination, or receiver, and the marker placed before the basic form of a verb
core_image: 手指向一个方向，箭头正指着目的地
scene: 站台上的人都盯着远处那一点，等那列火车开过来。 The crowd walked to the far end of the platform and waited.
sceneCN: 这里 to 是「往、到」（第 1 个义项：表示朝向或到达某处）；句意为人群走到站台尽头等着。画面有铁路、人群与远处车灯。

derivatives.zh: 加普通后缀 -ward 构成，义为「朝向」
toward 的英式变体，义为「朝向」
复合词，义为「在今天」
复合词，义为「今晚」

senses.title: Towards a place
senses.definition: in the direction of a place, with the idea of arrival
senses.definitionCN: 朝某地的方向，并含抵达之意
senses.example: They walked to the far end of the platform.
senses.exampleCN: 他们走到站台的另一端。
senses.why: The Old English preposition named motion toward a goal, and the goal being reached is the arrival sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语介词表示朝目标移动，抵达目标便成了「到」的义。

senses.title: As far as
senses.definition: used to show the limit or end of a movement or range
senses.definitionCN: 表示移动或范围的终点
senses.example: The queue stretched from the gate to the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍从大门一直排到街角。
senses.why: Direction plus limit gives a line that ends at a point.
senses.whyCN: 方向加界限，画出一条终于某点的线。

senses.title: The receiver of an action
senses.definition: used to introduce the person who receives something
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出接受某物的人
senses.example: Please give the letter to your teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 请把信交给你的老师。
senses.why: The goal of a movement is often a person, so the reaching word becomes the receiving word.
senses.whyCN: 移动目标常是一个人，因此「抵达」的词也成了「给予」的词。

senses.title: Showing a relationship
senses.definition: used to show a relationship between two things, such as comparison or attitude
senses.definitionCN: 表示两事物之间的关系，如比较或态度
senses.example: She is kind to strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 她对陌生人很和善。
senses.why: The goal of an attitude is the person or thing it is directed at.
senses.whyCN: 态度的指向就是它所对着的人或物。

senses.title: Telling the time
senses.definition: used in clock readings before the next hour
senses.definitionCN: 钟点表达中用于下一个整点之前
senses.example: It is ten to six.
senses.exampleCN: 现在五点五十（差十分六点）。
senses.why: Counting forward toward the coming hour is the direction sense applied to the clock face.
senses.whyCN: 朝着下一个小时数下去，就是方向义用在钟面上。

senses.title: Before the basic verb
senses.definition: the marker used before the basic form of a verb
senses.definitionCN: 放在动词原形前的标记
senses.example: He wants to leave now.
senses.exampleCN: 他现在想走。
senses.why: The old preposition of direction was placed before a verb to show the intended action, and became the infinitive marker.
senses.whyCN: 古英语表示方向的介词被放在动词前表示打算做的动作，后来成为不定式标记。

senses.title: Showing purpose
senses.definition: used to state the purpose of an action
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明动作的目的
senses.example: She came to say goodbye.
senses.exampleCN: 她是来道别的。
senses.why: Reaching toward an aim is the same movement, now aimed at an act rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 朝目标抵达的同一动作，此时目标是个行为而非地点。

senses.title: Closed or shut
senses.definition: used with door in the phrase to after door to mean shut
senses.definitionCN: 与门连用，表示关严
senses.example: Pull the door to when you leave.
senses.exampleCN: 离开时把门带上。
senses.why: Something that has moved right up to its frame is wholly closed.
senses.whyCN: 完全抵到门框的东西就彻底关上了。

senses.title: To and fro
senses.definition: used in the phrase to and fro for back-and-forth movement
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 to and fro，表示来回移动
senses.example: The pendulum swung to and fro.
senses.exampleCN: 钟摆来回摆动。
senses.why: Two opposite direction words paired give movement that never settles.
senses.whyCN: 两个相反方向的词配对，得到永远停不下的移动。

senses.title: According to
senses.definition: used in the phrase according to for a source of information
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 according to，表示信息来源
senses.example: According to the notice, the hall is closed.
senses.exampleCN: 根据告示，礼堂关闭。
senses.why: The information is measured against its source, which is the limit sense again.
senses.whyCN: 信息以其来源为界，又是界限义。

intro.en: The word is one of the oldest in the language, an Old English preposition of direction related to forms in other Germanic languages.
intro.cn: 这是语言中最古老的词之一，古英语中介词表示方向，与其它日耳曼语中的形式同源。

items.en: To meant toward, and also served to mark the person a thing was given to.
items.cn: 古英语 to 意为「朝向」，也用来标记接受某物的人。

items.en: Cognate forms in other Germanic languages carry the same direction sense.
items.cn: 其它日耳曼语中的同源形式带有同样的方向义。

items.en: The preposition was already used before a verb to express purpose.
items.cn: 这个介词已在动词前使用以表达目的。

items.en: Unstressed forms of the infinitive marker develop, giving the modern part of to.
items.cn: 不定式标记的弱读形式出现，成为现代 to 的一部分。

items.en: The unstressed pronunciation survives both as preposition and as infinitive marker.
items.cn: 弱读音在介词与不定式标记两种用法中都保留下来。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as to and fro and close to settle in the language.
items.cn: to and fro、close to 等固定短语在语言中定型。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words often confused with this spelling, while the near-meaning group lists other prepositions of direction.
note.cn: 形近组收集容易与本词拼写混淆的词，近义组列出其它表示方向的介词。

entries.definition: also, or to an excessive degree, a different word
entries.definitionCN: 也；太；只是读音相同，词源不同

entries.definition: the number after one, a different word
entries.definitionCN: 二；只是读音相同，词源不同

entries.definition: in the direction of
entries.definitionCN: 朝向

entries.definition: on this present day
entries.definitionCN: 在今天

entries.definition: moving so as to be inside
entries.definitionCN: 进入

entries.definition: moving so as to be on a surface
entries.definitionCN: 到……上面

entries.definition: in the direction of, the British variant
entries.definitionCN: 朝向

entries.definition: showing the starting point of a movement
entries.definitionCN: 从；自

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the single direction image, the fixed phrases, and the confusing twins.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「朝向」这一单一意象、固定短语与易混词入手。

normal.en: To, too, and two sound alike and behave quite differently.
normal.cn: to、too、two 读音相同而用法完全不同。

normal.en: From A to B draws the whole line; to alone marks only its end.
normal.cn: from A to B 画出整条线，单是 to 只标出终点。

normal.en: The infinitive to appears where purpose or direction points at a verb.
normal.cn: 不定式 to 出现的地方，方向正指向一个动词。

normal.en: Ten to six counts up to the coming hour.
normal.cn: ten to six 是朝着下一个整点数。

normal.en: To and fro is a pair that never settles on a direction.
normal.cn: to and fro 是一对永远定不下来的方向。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow drawn plainly from one dot to another.
abstract.cn: 想象一支清晰的箭，从一个点指向另一个点。

abstract.en: Think of a door pushed right up against its frame.
abstract.cn: 想一扇门被推到紧贴门框。

abstract.en: The little word is the shortest road between two words.
abstract.cn: 这个小词是两个词之间最短的一条路。

examples.en: We drove to the coast and back in one day.
examples.cn: 我们一天之内开车去了海边又回来。

examples.en: She gave the note to her brother.
examples.cn: 她把纸条给了弟弟。

examples.en: He turned to look at the clock.
examples.cn: 他转过身去看钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「土」——一路走到土里去，方向指得明明白白。

root: 古英语 to（朝向、到），日耳曼语族最古老的介词之一，与其它日耳曼语同源词同义；不定式标记由「朝向某个动作」的用法发展而来。

sensesIntro.en: Everything comes from pointing at a goal: a place, a limit, a receiver, an attitude, a coming hour, a verb to be done, or a purpose to be served.
sensesIntro.cn: 一切都源于「指向目标」：地点、界限、受者、态度、下一个整点、要做的动词，或要达成的目的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow pointing from where you are to a goal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支箭从所在之处指向目标。

branches.en: Direction and the place it ends.
branches.cn: 方向及其结束的地点。

branches.en: The receiver of a gift or an attitude.
branches.cn: 礼物或态度的接受者。

branches.en: Counting toward an hour and measuring against a source.
branches.cn: 朝整点数，以及依据来源衡量。

branches.en: Pointing at a verb or a purpose.
branches.cn: 指向动词或目的。

branches.en: Reaching the frame, and moving back and forth.
branches.cn: 抵到门框，以及来回移动。

intro.en: This function word has no real affixes, but it forms compounds and takes a regular weak pronunciation.
intro.cn: 这个功能词没有真正的词缀，但会组成复合词，并有规律的弱读形式。

latinIntro.en: To is Germanic and not borrowed, so the Latin list is empty apart from comparison words.
latinIntro.cn: to 是日耳曼语词，不是借词，因此拉丁表仅列对照词。

items.example: The whole word is the root.
Today and tonight are compounds of this sort.

items.exampleCN: today 把 to 与 day 连起来。
tonight 把 to 与 night 连起来。

items.example: Into adds the idea of entering.
Onto adds the idea of a surface.

definition_zh: 价值；价格；重要性；重视；估量
definition_en: the worth of something in money or in importance, or to think highly of it
core_image: 旧货商把一只旧表端在手里，翻看背面刻字
scene: 旧货铺里，老板把一只黄铜表翻过来，看背面的刻字和磨损，然后才报出一个数。 The dealer set a value of two hundred on the watch.
sceneCN: 这里 value 是「价值、估价」（第 1 个义项：值多少）；句意为旧货商给那只表估了两百。端表翻看的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加 -able 构成形容词，义为「有价值的」
加 in- 与 -able 构成，义为「无价的」
加 -ation 构成名词，义为「估价」
加 -less 构成，义为「毫无价值的」

senses.title: Worth in money
senses.definition: the amount of money something is worth or would sell for
senses.definitionCN: 某物值多少钱或能卖多少钱
senses.example: The value of the house has doubled in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子十年间价值翻了一倍。
senses.why: Latin valere meant to be worth, and the noun first names what a thing can be exchanged for.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 valere 意为「值得」，这个名词最初指一件东西能换来的那个数目。

senses.title: Worth in importance
senses.definition: the importance or usefulness of something that is not for sale
senses.definitionCN: 某些非卖品的重要性或用处
senses.example: The value of the trip lay in the people she met.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟旅行的价值在于她遇见的人。
senses.why: If worth can be counted, it need not be counted in coins, so the word moves to things that are priceless.
senses.whyCN: 既然「值」可以计量，就不必只以钱币计量，于是词义挪到了无价之物上。

senses.title: To think highly of something
senses.definition: to consider something important and worth keeping
senses.definitionCN: 认为某物重要、值得保留
senses.example: He values his friends more than his salary.
senses.exampleCN: 他看重朋友胜过薪水。
senses.why: To see worth in something is to prize it, so the noun becomes a verb of holding dear.
senses.whyCN: 看出一件事的价值就是看重它，于是名词转成了表示珍惜的动词。

senses.title: To estimate the worth of something
senses.definition: to work out how much money something is worth
senses.definitionCN: 算定某物值多少钱
senses.example: The house was valued at a lower figure last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子去年的估价更低。
senses.why: The other verb use keeps the money sense: to value is to put a figure on what something is worth.
senses.whyCN: 动词的另一用法保留了钱款义：value 就是给某物定一个价。

senses.title: A belief about what matters
senses.definition: in the plural, the beliefs a person or group holds about right and wrong
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式指个人或群体对是非的观念
senses.example: The school says it teaches traditional values.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校称它教授传统观念。
senses.why: The things a group prizes are its values, so the plural names beliefs rather than prices.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体所看重的东西就是它的 values，因此复数指观念而不是价格。

intro.en: The Latin root of worth, borrowed through French as a noun and then turned into a verb in English.
intro.cn: 拉丁语「值得」的词根，经法语借入作名词，后在英语中转为动词。

items.en: Valere meant to be strong or to be worth, and valor named worth and courage.
items.cn: valere 意为「强壮、值得」，valor 指价值与勇气。

items.en: The feminine participle valuta meant a thing worth so much.
items.cn: 阴性分词 valuta 意为「值若干的东西」。

items.en: French valoir and the noun value carried the sense of worth into use.
items.cn: 法语 valoir 与名词 value 把「值」这一意义带入使用。

items.en: English borrows value as a noun of price and worth.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 value，作价格与价值的名词。

items.en: The verb senses of prizing and pricing grow, and the plural values names beliefs.
items.cn: 表示珍视与估价的动词义发展起来，复数 values 指观念。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the worth family, and the near-meaning group sets worth against price and cost.
note.cn: 形近组收集表示「值」的词族，近义组把价值与价格、成本放在一起。

entries.definition: worth a lot
entries.definitionCN: 有价值的；贵重的

entries.definition: legally or logically sound
entries.definitionCN: 有效的；站得住脚的

entries.definition: an estimate of worth
entries.definitionCN: 估价

entries.definition: courage in battle
entries.definitionCN: 英勇

entries.definition: the native word for value
entries.definitionCN: 价值（英语本土词）

entries.definition: the money asked for goods
entries.definitionCN: 价格

entries.definition: what is given up to get something
entries.definitionCN: 成本

entries.definition: worth of a good quality
entries.definitionCN: 优点；价值

normalIntro.en: One noun covers both the price on a tag and the worth a person refuses to sell.
normalIntro.cn: 一个名词同时覆盖标签上的价格与人情里不肯出售的价值。

normal.en: Value for money is the standard phrase in shopping and reviews.
normal.cn: value for money 是购物与评测中的标准说法。

normal.en: Values in the plural means beliefs, not prices.
normal.cn: 复数 values 指观念，不是价格。

normal.en: The verb takes both frames: value a friend, value a house.
normal.cn: 这个动词两种框架都用：value a friend 与 value a house。

normal.en: Valuable and invaluable look like opposites but are not.
normal.cn: valuable 与 invaluable 看着像反义，其实不是。

normal.en: Valuation is the formal word from the same stem.
normal.cn: valuation 是同词干上的正式名词。

abstract.en: Picture a dealer turning a brass watch to read the engraving.
abstract.cn: 想象旧货商翻过黄铜表看刻字。

abstract.en: See a friend keep a letter that has no price at all.
abstract.cn: 看朋友留着一封无从标价的信。

abstract.en: Hear a school claim it teaches old-fashioned values.
abstract.cn: 听一所学校说它教老式的观念。

examples.en: The value of the land rose sharply after the road was built.
examples.cn: 修路之后这块地的价值猛涨。

examples.en: She values honesty more than politeness.
examples.cn: 她看重诚实胜过礼貌。

examples.en: The painting was valued at ten thousand pounds.
examples.cn: 这幅画被估价一万英镑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为留」——有价值的东西才值得为之留下来。

root: 拉丁语 valere（值得、强壮）的阴性分词 valuta（价值），经古法语 value 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: The core of worth gives money, then importance, then the two verbs of prizing and pricing, and finally the beliefs people hold.
sensesIntro.cn: 「值得」这个核心先给出钱款，再给出重要性，再给出珍视与估价两个动词，最后给出人们所持的观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dealer turning a brass watch in his hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧货商手里翻看一只黄铜表。

branches.en: The price branch: a figure on a tag.
branches.cn: 价格分支：标签上的数字。

branches.en: The meaning branch: worth without a price.
branches.cn: 意义分支：无价的价值。

branches.en: The holding branch: friendship kept above salary.
branches.cn: 持有分支：友情重于薪水。

branches.en: The pricing branch: an expert puts a number on it.
branches.cn: 定价分支：专家给出一个数字。

branches.en: The belief branch: shared ideas of what matters.
branches.cn: 观念分支：共同认定的重要之事。

intro.en: A Latin root of worth carried into English through French, later hosting a crowd of suffixes.
intro.cn: 一个表示「值得」的拉丁词根经法语进入英语，后来又接上了一大串后缀。

latinIntro.en: Valere, to be worth, gives valuta; French shortens it to value, and English takes value as both noun and verb.
latinIntro.cn: valere（值得）给出 valuta；法语缩为 value，英语把 value 同时用作名词与动词。

items.example: The root covers worth and strength together.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根同时覆盖价值与强壮。

items.example: The ending shows a borrowed noun.
items.exampleCN: 这一词尾显示是借入名词。

items.example: Worth and value answer each other.
items.exampleCN: worth 与 value 彼此对应。

latinEntries.meaning: to be worth, to be strong

definition_zh: 抓住；接住；赶上（车）；染上（病）；引起注意
definition_en: to take hold of something moving, to stop and hold it, to board in time, or to get an illness
core_image: 伸出手，在东西飞走的瞬间把它按住
scene: 体育课的自由活动时间，男生们在操场上练习接球。 During break the boys practised how to catch a high ball on the playground.
sceneCN: 这里 catch 是「接住」（第 1 个义项：伸手接住移动之物）；句意为课间在操场练接高球。

derivatives.zh: 由 catch 加 -er 构成，义为「接球手；捕手」
由 catch 加 -ing 构成，义为「传染性的；动人的」

senses.title: To take hold of something moving
senses.definition: to stop and hold something that is moving or falling
senses.definitionCN: 截住并握住移动或坠落之物
senses.example: He caught the ball with one hand.
senses.exampleCN: 他单手接住了球。
senses.why: The word grew from chasing: to catch is to reach the thing that tries to leave.
senses.whyCN: 此词由「追逐」生长：接住，就是追上那个想逃的东西。

senses.title: To reach a bus, train or person in time
senses.definition: to arrive in time for a bus, train or meeting
senses.definitionCN: 及时到达以乘上车或见到人
senses.example: We ran to catch the last bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们跑去赶末班车。
senses.why: Chasing does not always mean grabbing; sometimes just boarding in time.
senses.whyCN: 追逐未必动手，有时只是及时登上一班车。

senses.title: To get an illness
senses.definition: to become ill with a disease that spreads
senses.definitionCN: 染上会传染的病
senses.example: She caught a cold in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她在雨里着凉感冒了。
senses.why: A disease moves from person to person like something that leaps and must be seized.
senses.whyCN: 疾病在人间跳来跳去，像非要抓住不可的东西。

senses.title: To draw attention
senses.definition: to attract the eye or interest
senses.definitionCN: 把目光或兴趣吸引过来
senses.example: A red scarf caught my eye.
senses.exampleCN: 一条红围巾吸引了我。
senses.why: The eye too reaches out and seizes what glides past it.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛也会伸手，一把抓住掠过的东西。

senses.title: To trap or entangle
senses.definition: to become stuck or tangled in something
senses.definitionCN: 被某物卡住或缠住
senses.example: His sleeve caught on the door handle.
senses.exampleCN: 他的袖子被门把手钩住了。
senses.why: What is seized may simply be held fast, stuck like a fish in a net.
senses.whyCN: 被抓住的东西只是被扣住，像网中的鱼。

intro.en: Catch began as a hunter's word for chasing down prey.
intro.cn: catch 起初是猎人追捕猎物的用词。

items.en: Old North French cachier meant to chase.
items.cn: 古法语北部方言 cachier 意为追逐。

items.en: It descends from Latin captare, to try to seize, a frequentative of capere.
items.cn: 其源自拉丁语 captare（设法抓取），是 capere 的反复动词。

items.en: Norse ketcha reinforced the English form and its chase sense.
items.cn: 诺斯语 ketcha 强化了英语的词形与追逐义。

items.en: Middle English catch meant to pursue, seize and trap.
items.cn: 中古英语 catch 兼指追、抓与困住。

items.en: Modern catch added buses, colds and attention.
items.cn: 现代 catch 又添赶车、感冒与吸引诸义。

note.en: The first group collects look-alike words; the second collects seizing verbs.
note.cn: 第一组收形近词，第二组收抓取类动词。

entries.definition: To look at; a timepiece.
entries.definitionCN: 动词/名词，义为「观看；手表」，尾音与 catch 相近。

entries.definition: A game, or a thing that goes well with another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「比赛；相配之物」，拼写与 catch 相近。

entries.definition: To take by force.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「捕获」，与 catch 同出拉丁词根。

entries.definition: To seize suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抓取」，动作急促。

entries.definition: To take hold quickly and firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抓住」，书面感强。

entries.definition: To fail to catch or hit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「错过；没接住」，是反义对照。

normalIntro.en: Remember catch as the chaser's success.
normalIntro.cn: 把 catch 记成追逐者的成功一刻。

normal.en: catch comes from cachier, to chase.
normal.cn: catch 源自 cachier（追逐）。

normal.en: capture shares the Latin root capere.
normal.cn: capture 与 catch 同享拉丁词根 capere。

normal.en: caught is its past tense, said like court.
normal.cn: caught 是过去式，读音近似 court。

normal.en: catch a cold is a fixed phrase.
normal.cn: catch a cold 是固定搭配。

normal.en: catch up with means to reach from behind.
normal.cn: catch up with 即从后面追上。

abstract.en: Stretch one hand toward a flying ball.
abstract.cn: 伸手迎向飞来的球。

abstract.en: Run down a platform, one step behind the bus.
abstract.cn: 在站台狂奔，离车一步之遥。

abstract.en: Feel a sneeze tickle before the cold lands.
abstract.cn: 喷嚏在感冒落地前先痒了一下。

examples.en: The dog caught the frisbee in mid-air.
examples.cn: 狗在半空接住了飞盘。

examples.en: Hurry, or we won't catch the train.
examples.cn: 快点，不然赶不上火车了。

examples.en: His joke caught everyone's attention.
examples.cn: 他的玩笑吸引了所有人的注意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凯奇」——影星凯奇总是伸手接住飞来的道具。

root: 拉丁语 capere（抓取）→ captare（设法抓）→ 古法语 cachier（追逐）→ 英语 catch；同根词 capture、capable、accept。

sensesIntro.en: Catch moves from seizing what flees to boarding in time, catching cold and catching the eye.
sensesIntro.cn: catch 从抓逃跑之物出发，长出赶车、染病与吸引目光诸义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing on something that will not wait
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手合拢，扣住不再等待之物

branches.en: Balls, fish and thieves
branches.cn: 球、鱼与窃贼

branches.en: Buses and trains in time
branches.cn: 及时赶上的车

branches.en: Colds and other germs
branches.cn: 感冒与病菌

branches.en: Eyes caught by colour
branches.cn: 被颜色勾住的目光

branches.en: Sleeves stuck on handles
branches.cn: 钩在把手上的衣袖

intro.en: Catch keeps the Latin seize-root capere visible in its cousins.
intro.cn: catch 的拉丁「抓取」词根 capere 在其同族词中清晰可见。

latinIntro.en: From capere English gained capture, capable and accept.
latinIntro.cn: 从 capere 派生出英语的 capture、capable 与 accept。

items.example: Capere is the old hunter's verb.

items.exampleCN: captare 指一次次试图抓住。

definition_zh: 举止；表现；守规矩；（机器、物质）表现
definition_en: to act in a particular way, or to act in a polite and controlled way
core_image: 孩子在客人面前坐直身子，把双手放在膝盖上
scene: 家里来了客人，妈妈低声提醒孩子坐好。 The children behaved well at the dinner table.
sceneCN: 这里 behave 是「守规矩、表现好」（第 2 个义项：举止得体、听话）；句意为孩子们在餐桌旁表现得很有礼貌。

derivatives.zh: 由 behave 加 -iour 构成，义为「行为；举止」，美式拼作 behavior
由 behaviour 加 -al 构成，义为「行为的」
由 mis-「不当」加 behave 构成，义为「行为不端」
由 well 与 behaved 组合而成，义为「表现好的、听话的」

senses.title: To act in a certain way
senses.definition: to act or conduct oneself in a particular way, whether good or bad
senses.definitionCN: 以某种特定方式行动或表现自己，不论好坏
senses.example: He behaved strangely at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 他在聚会上举止古怪。
senses.why: Old English behabban joined be-, meaning around or for, with habban, to have, so the verb meant to hold or carry oneself, and that is the general sense of acting.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 behabban 由表「在周围、为了」的 be- 与表「持有」的 habban 组成，本义是「把自己拿住」，也就是一般意义上的「举止行事」。

senses.title: To act politely and properly
senses.definition: to act in a polite, controlled way that others approve of
senses.definitionCN: 以有礼貌、有节制、别人认可的方式行事
senses.example: The children behaved well at dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在晚饭时表现很好。
senses.why: Holding oneself in hand is also the picture of good manners, so the general sense narrowed into the everyday sense of behaving properly.
senses.whyCN: 「把自己管住」也正是有教养的样子，于是宽泛的「举止」义收窄成了日常说的「守规矩、表现好」。

senses.title: For a machine or material to perform
senses.definition: for a machine, system, or substance to act or work in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 指机器、系统或物质以某种方式运作或起作用
senses.example: The new engine behaves well in cold weather.
senses.exampleCN: 新发动机在寒冷天气里表现良好。
senses.why: The way a person controls himself is projected onto machines: how a thing conducts itself under conditions is simply how it works.
senses.whyCN: 人控制自己的方式被挪到机器上：某物在特定条件下「自处」的方式，就是它的运作状况。

senses.title: To control oneself
senses.definition: used reflexively in behave oneself, meaning to act properly and stay under control
senses.definitionCN: 用于 behave oneself 这一反身结构，义为举止得体、保持自我约束
senses.example: Behave yourself in front of the guests.
senses.exampleCN: 在客人面前要守规矩。
senses.why: The reflexive form turns the old image of holding oneself back toward the speaker, making self-control the explicit point.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把「把自己拿住」这个老画面转回说话人自身，让「自我约束」成为明确的意思。

intro.en: Behave began as a compound of be- and have, literally to hold oneself.
intro.cn: behave 最初是 be- 与 have 的复合词，字面意思是「把自己拿住」。

items.en: Old English behabban joined be-, meaning around or for, with habban, meaning to have or hold.
items.cn: 古英语 behabban 由 be-「在周围、为了」与 habban「持有」组成。

items.en: The compound literally meant to hold oneself, that is, to keep oneself under control.
items.cn: 这个复合词字面意为「把握住自己」，也就是「把自己控制在手里」。

items.en: The verb passed into Middle English with the sense of conducting oneself in some way.
items.cn: 这个动词进入中古英语，意思是「以某种方式自处、行事」。

items.en: From conduct in general came the narrower sense of good conduct, and from people came the use for machines and materials.
items.cn: 从一般的「行为」分出较窄的「好行为」，又从人身上扩展到机器与材料。

items.en: Modern English uses behave for conduct in general, for good manners, and for the way things work.
items.cn: 现代英语里 behave 可指一般举止、良好教养，也可指事物的运作表现。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family forms and the mis- compound; the near-meaning group collects verbs that are close to acting or conducting oneself.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的各种形式与 mis- 复合词；近义组收与「行事、举止」相近的动词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to possess, which is the second half of behave.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拥有」，是 behave 的后半部分来源。

entries.definition: The noun for conduct; it spells behavior in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行为、举止」，美式拼作 behavior。

entries.definition: The regular past tense and past participle.
entries.definitionCN: 规则过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: To behave badly, formed with the prefix mis-.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「行为不端」，由前缀 mis- 构成。

entries.definition: To do something or to conduct oneself in a way; the closest general synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「行动、表现」，是最接近的一般同义词。

entries.definition: To organize an activity, or to behave in a particular way, in formal use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，正式用法中义为「进行、表现」，也指组织某项活动。

entries.definition: To carry out an action or to work in a particular way; it matches the machine sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「执行、表现」，对应机器义项。

entries.definition: To act in response to something, a narrower kind of behaving.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「作出反应」，是较窄的一种「表现」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded compound parts, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的复合成分、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Be- means around or for, and have means hold: to hold oneself is to behave.
normal.cn: be- 表示「在周围、为了」，have 表示「持有」：把自己拿住就是 behave。

normal.en: Behaviour is the noun, misbehave is the bad verb, and well-behaved is the adjective.
normal.cn: behaviour 是名词，misbehave 是表示「行为不端」的动词，well-behaved 是形容词。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with well, badly, like and oneself.
normal.cn: 它常与 well、badly、like、oneself 搭配。

normal.en: The endings are simple: -s, -ing and -ed, with no doubling of the final e.
normal.cn: 词尾变化很简单：加 -s、-ing、-ed，末尾的 e 不与词干重复。

normal.en: Spell be plus have: two common words joined, and the e in the middle is kept.
normal.cn: 拼写是 be 加 have：两个常见词拼在一起，中间的 e 保留。

abstract.en: See a child sitting straight with both hands on the knees: holding oneself made visible.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子坐直、双手放在膝盖上：把「拿住自己」变成看得见的姿势。

abstract.en: Move the same picture to an engine and it becomes the machine sense of performing.
abstract.cn: 把同一幅画挪到发动机上，就成了机器「表现如何」的义项。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the straight-backed posture bring conduct back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让坐直的姿势把「举止」带回来。

examples.en: He behaved strangely at the party.
examples.cn: 他在聚会上举止古怪。

examples.en: The children behaved well at dinner.
examples.cn: 孩子们在晚饭时表现很好。

examples.en: The new engine behaves well in cold weather.
examples.cn: 新发动机在寒冷天气里表现良好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必嘿」——在客人面前必嘿地笑，举止得体：举止

root: behave 来自古英语 behabban，由 be-「在周围、为了」加 habban「持有」合成，本义是「把自己拿住」。由「控制自身」引申出一般举止，再分出「守规矩」一义；后来这个「自处的方式」又被用到机器和物质上，表示「表现、性能如何」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of behave rest on one picture: holding oneself, whether in public, in good manners, inside a machine, or before oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: behave 的四个义项都立在同一个画面上：「把自己拿住」，无论是在众人面前、在礼数上、在机器内部，还是面对自己。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child sitting straight with both hands on the knees
core.cn: 核心意象：一个坐得笔直、双手放在膝盖上的孩子

branches.en: THE GENERAL WAY: holding oneself becomes the neutral sense of acting in some way.
branches.cn: 一般举止线：把自己拿住，变成中性的「以某种方式行事」。

branches.en: THE MANNERS: the same control narrows into acting politely and properly.
branches.cn: 礼仪线：同一种控制收窄成有礼貌、守规矩地行事。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the human picture moves onto engines and materials as how they perform.
branches.cn: 物体线：人的画面挪到发动机与材料上，成为它们的「表现」。

branches.en: THE REFLEXIVE: behave oneself turns the control back toward the speaker.
branches.cn: 反身线：behave oneself 把这份控制转回说话人自身。

branches.en: THE TWO LEVELS: the same verb covers plain conduct and the narrower idea of good conduct.
branches.cn: 两层线：同一个动词既指普通的举止，也指较窄的「好行为」。

intro.en: Behave is a fused compound, so the items below are its old parts, its inflections, and the suffixes that built its family.
intro.cn: behave 是粘合的复合词，下面列出的是它的古老构件、屈折形式和构成词族的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere, to have or hold, shares an older Indo-European root with the second half of behave, but it was not borrowed into the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habere「持有」与 behave 的后半部分同出更早的印欧词根，但并非直接借入。

items.exampleCN: 它是 behave 的第一个成分。

items.example: It is the second element of behave.

definition_zh: 拍手；鼓掌；轻拍；啪的一声；拍（手）
definition_en: to hit your hands together to show approval; to strike lightly with an open hand; the sound made
core_image: 两只手掌合拢发出的清脆响声
scene: 演出结束时，全场观众一起拍起手来。 Everyone clapped loudly at the end of the show.
sceneCN: 这里 clap 是「鼓掌」（第 1 个义项：双手相击表示赞许）；句意是演出结束时大家热烈鼓掌。

derivatives.zh: 同义近亲词，义为「鼓掌欢迎；称赞」
同族词，义为「掌声；喝彩」
由 clap 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「钟锤；拍板」

senses.title: To hit the hands together in praise
senses.definition: to bring the hands together loudly to show approval
senses.definitionCN: 双手合击发出响声以示赞许
senses.example: The students clapped for the winners.
senses.exampleCN: 同学们为获胜者鼓掌。
senses.why: Hands meeting in joy are the basic picture of the word.
senses.whyCN: 双手因喜悦相击，是这个词的基本画面。

senses.title: To strike lightly with the open hand
senses.definition: to touch someone or something quickly with an open hand
senses.definitionCN: 用张开的手掌快速轻触某人或某物
senses.example: She clapped a hat on his head.
senses.exampleCN: 她把帽子轻扣在他头上。
senses.why: The hand's flat hit extends to touching things with it.
senses.whyCN: 手掌的平击动作延伸到用它轻触事物。

senses.title: A loud sudden single sound
senses.definition: a sudden loud noise, especially of thunder
senses.definitionCN: 突然的巨响，尤指雷声
senses.example: A clap of thunder woke the whole house.
senses.exampleCN: 一声炸雷惊醒了全家。
senses.why: One hand-clap sounds like one thunder-crack.
senses.whyCN: 一声掌声与一声炸雷相似，义项由此而来。

senses.title: The sound or act of clapping
senses.definition: the noise made when hands strike together
senses.definitionCN: 双手相击发出的声音
senses.example: Claps echoed through the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 掌声在大厅里回荡。
senses.why: The action names its own sound.
senses.whyCN: 动作直接命名了自己的声音。

intro.en: Clap is a native English word that simply imitates its own sound.
intro.cn: clap 是英语固有词，单纯模仿自身的声音。

items.en: Old English clappian meant to clap or to beat.
items.cn: 古英语 clappian 义为「拍打」。

items.en: It belongs to a Germanic group of echo words like Dutch klappen.
items.cn: 它属于日耳曼拟声词群，如荷兰语 klappen。

items.en: Middle English kept clap for both striking and applauding.
items.cn: 中古英语 clap 兼指击打与鼓掌。

items.en: Modern English kept the verb and grew the noun uses.
items.cn: 现代英语保留动词并发展出名词用法。

items.en: The thunder sense appeared as the word spread to loud cracks.
items.cn: 随词义扩展到巨大爆裂声，产生了雷声义项。

note.en: The first group gathers hand-hit words; the second gathers look-alikes.
note.cn: 第一组收拍击类词，第二组收形近词。

entries.definition: To hold tightly; a fastener.
entries.definitionCN: 动词/名词，义为「紧握；搭扣」，拼写与 clap 接近。

entries.definition: The sharp nail of an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「爪子」，词首与 clap 相同。

entries.definition: A hit with the flat of the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 名词/动词，义为「掌掴」，词尾与 clap 相同。

entries.definition: To clap to praise.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「鼓掌称赞」，较正式。

entries.definition: The sound of clapping.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「掌声」。

entries.definition: The loud sound after lightning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「雷声」，与 clap 的巨响义相关。

normalIntro.en: Remember clap by sound imitation and family.
normalIntro.cn: 通过拟声和词族记忆 clap。

normal.en: clap sounds like two hands meeting.
normal.cn: clap 读起来就像双手相击。

normal.en: applause is the longer formal noun.
normal.cn: applause 是更正式的名词。

normal.en: double the p before -ed: clapped.
normal.cn: 加 -ed 前双写 p，写作 clapped。

normal.cn: a clap of thunder 是固定短语。

normal.cn: slap 与 clap 共用 -ap 词尾。

abstract.en: Feel two palms meet in one bright crack.
abstract.cn: 感受双掌相击的一声脆响。

abstract.en: See hands rising in rows after the song.
abstract.cn: 想象歌声结束后成排举起的手。

abstract.en: Hear thunder split the sky with a single crack.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见雷声劈开天空的一声爆响。

examples.en: Please clap along with the music.
examples.cn: 请跟着音乐拍手。

examples.en: We gave the actors a big clap.
examples.cn: 我们为演员们热烈鼓掌。

examples.en: The room was full of claps and cheers.
examples.cn: 房间里满是掌声和欢呼。

sensesIntro.en: Clap starts with two hands meeting, then spreads to light hits and loud cracks.
sensesIntro.cn: clap 从双手相击出发，延伸到轻拍动作和炸雷巨响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two palms meeting in a bright crack
core.cn: 核心意象：双掌相击发出清脆一响

branches.en: Applauding with hands
branches.cn: 鼓掌赞许

branches.en: Touching with a flat hand
branches.cn: 张开手掌轻拍

branches.cn: 突然的巨响

intro.cn: clap 属拟声词，词族建立在 -ap 回声上。
