definition_zh: 向上；起来；在上面；（数量）上升；（时间）到；完成；沿……而上
definition_en: towards a higher place, position, or level, or into an active or finished state
core_image: 一只手从低处把东西往上托
scene: 工地上吊绳绷紧，一捆钢筋从坑底慢慢露出地面。 The load came up out of the pit slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 up 是「向上」（第 1 个义项：由低处升高处）；句意为那捆货从坑底慢慢升上来。一只手从低处把东西往上托，正是这个词的核心。

pos.zh: 向上的；已完成的；醒着的

derivatives.zh: 由 up 加比较级词尾构成，义为「上部的；较高的」
由 up 加 -ward 构成，义为「向上的；朝上」
由 up 与 stairs 复合，义为「在楼上；上楼」
由 up 与 set 复合，原义「打翻」，引申为「使心烦」

senses.title: Towards a higher place
senses.definition: towards a higher place or position
senses.definitionCN: 朝更高的地方或位置
senses.example: She looked up at the clock and frowned.
senses.exampleCN: 她抬头看了看钟，皱起眉头。
senses.why: The word began as a Germanic adverb of upward motion, and that physical direction is still its centre.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是日耳曼语中表示向上运动的副词，这一物理方向至今仍是它的中心。

senses.title: Into a standing or active state
senses.definition: into a standing, awake, or working state
senses.definitionCN: 进入站起、醒着或运转的状态
senses.example: He got up as soon as the bell rang.
senses.exampleCN: 铃声一响他就站了起来。
senses.why: Rising from the ground is also rising into activity, so standing up and waking up share one word.
senses.whyCN: 从地面升起也就是进入活动状态，因此「站起来」与「醒来」共用一个词。

senses.title: Along a road or a slope
senses.definition: used as a preposition for movement along or higher on something
senses.definitionCN: 作介词，表示沿某物前行或在其较高处
senses.example: They walked up the hill without speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一言不发地走上山坡。
senses.why: Walking up a slope is the same upward motion, so the adverb easily becomes a preposition of route.
senses.whyCN: 沿坡行走还是同一个向上的动作，因此这个副词很容易转为表示路径的介词。

senses.title: Increasing in number or level
senses.definition: used of prices, numbers, or levels that rise
senses.definitionCN: 用于价格、数字或水平的升高
senses.example: Sales went up sharply in the last quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 上季度销量急剧上升。
senses.why: Numbers move in space in everyday speech, so a rising figure is simply a thing that goes up.
senses.whyCN: 日常说法里数字也在空间中移动，于是数值上升就是一样东西「往上去了」。

senses.title: Finished or out of time
senses.definition: used when a period or supply has come to its end
senses.definitionCN: 表示一段时间或供给已经到尽头
senses.example: Time is up, so put your pens down.
senses.exampleCN: 时间到了，把笔放下吧。
senses.why: A measure filled to the top can rise no further, and that image gives the sense of finished.
senses.whyCN: 容器装到顶就再升不上去了，这个意象生出「结束、用完」的意思。

senses.title: As far as a stated number
senses.definition: used with to for the greatest number reached
senses.definitionCN: 与 to 连用，表示所达到的最大数目
senses.example: The hall holds up to three hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅最多能容纳三百人。
senses.why: If up means reaching a point higher on a scale, then up to names the point where a number stops.
senses.whyCN: 既然 up 指沿某一刻度到达更高处，那么 up to 就指出数字停下的那一点。

intro.en: One of the oldest words in English, an adverb of place before it was anything else.
intro.cn: 英语中最古老的词之一，它首先是表示方位的副词。

items.en: The reconstructed form upp means up, and it has relatives in Dutch and German.
items.cn: 重构形式 upp 意为「向上」，在荷兰语和德语中都有同源词。

items.en: The adverb up is recorded early, with the comparative upper forming alongside it.
items.cn: 副词 up 很早就有记录，比较级 upper 也随之形成。

items.en: It is used with verbs of motion, as in standan up, to stand up.
items.cn: 它常与运动动词连用，如 standan up（站起来）。

items.en: Everyday phrases such as get up and up to now fix the word as a particle.
items.cn: get up、up to now 这类日常短语把它固定为小品词。

items.en: The sense of finished or used up appears in time is up and the gas is up.
items.cn: 「结束、用完」的含义出现在 time is up 与 the gas is up 这类说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and derivatives of up, while the near-meaning group compares direction and degree words.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 up 的复合词与派生词，近义组比较方向与程度词。

entries.definition: higher of two things
entries.definitionCN: 上面的；较高的

entries.definition: moving towards a higher point
entries.definitionCN: 向上的

entries.definition: on or to a higher floor
entries.definitionCN: 在楼上；上楼

entries.definition: on top of
entries.definitionCN: 在……之上

entries.definition: in a higher position
entries.definitionCN: 在……上方

entries.definition: across or higher than
entries.definitionCN: 越过；在上方

entries.definition: towards a lower place
entries.definitionCN: 向下

entries.definition: high in the air
entries.definitionCN: 在高处

normalIntro.en: A tiny word with a very long history, best learned through its verb phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 一个历史极悠久的小词，最好的记法是通过它与动词组成的短语。

normal.en: Learn up through verbs: get up, look up, stand up, give up.
normal.cn: 通过动词记：get up、look up、stand up、give up。

normal.en: Up plus to means as far as, either in number or in time.
normal.cn: up 加 to 意为「达到」，可用于数目或时间。

normal.en: Upper is the older comparative of up, not a separate root.
normal.cn: upper 是 up 较古老的比较级，并非另一个词根。

normal.en: Up and down together make the picture of repeated movement.
normal.cn: up and down 连用画出反复移动的画面。

normal.en: Time is up uses up as finished, not as direction.
normal.cn: time is up 里的 up 表示「结束」，不是方向。

abstract.en: Watch a hand lift something out of a pit.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把东西从坑里托出来。

abstract.en: Feel a rope tighten and a bucket rise.
abstract.cn: 体会绳子绷紧、桶子升起。

abstract.en: See a hand switch a lamp on.
abstract.cn: 看一只手把灯打开。

examples.en: The children ran up the hill to see the sea.
examples.cn: 孩子们跑上山去看海。

examples.en: Prices went up again in the spring.
examples.cn: 价格在春天又一次上涨。

examples.en: Time is up, and the exam papers must be handed in.
examples.cn: 时间到了，试卷必须交上来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普」——搬东西时喊着阿普阿普，众人一起用力把重物往上抬。

root: 古英语 up（副词），源自日耳曼语重构形式 upp，与荷兰语 op、德语 auf 同源，本义「向上」

sensesIntro.en: One upward motion supplies direction, then standing, then rising levels, finally finishing and reaching a limit.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个向上的动作先给方向，再给站立，再给上升，最后给结束与达到极限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifting something from below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从下面把东西抬起。

branches.en: The direction branch: eyes and objects go higher.
branches.cn: 方向分支：视线与物件往高处去。

branches.en: The state branch: up means awake, standing, working.
branches.cn: 状态分支：up 指醒着、站着、运转着。

branches.en: The preposition branch: along or higher on a road.
branches.cn: 介词分支：沿路而行或位于高处。

branches.en: The figure branch: numbers that keep climbing.
branches.cn: 数字分支：一路往上爬的数值。

branches.en: The limit branch: used up, and as far as a number.
branches.cn: 极限分支：用完了，以及达到某个数目。

intro.en: A bare Germanic adverb that now works as particle, preposition, adjective, and noun.
intro.cn: 一个光秃秃的日耳曼语副词，如今可作小品词、介词、形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin expresses the same direction with sursum, upward, and the prefix super-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 sursum（向上）与前缀 super- 表达同一方向。

items.meaning: to raise to a better level

definition_zh: 价值；值……钱；值得；有用；财产
definition_en: the value of something in money or in importance, or deserving of something
core_image: 秤盘上放一件旧东西，指针停在一个谁都说不上来的刻度
scene: 旧货摊上，摊主看了看那只表，摇了摇头说这表不值几个钱，但时间准得让人舍不得扔。 The old bicycle is not worth much, but I would not sell it for anything.
sceneCN: 这里 worth 是「价值、值（多少钱）」（第 1 个义项：事物在金钱或重要性上可衡量的价值）；句意为这辆旧自行车不值多少钱，但我多少钱也不卖。秤盘上那件东西停在一个不好说的刻度上，就是这个词的印象。

collocations.zh: 不管有没有用；仅供参考

derivatives.zh: 由 worth 加 -y 构成，义为「值得的；可敬的」
由 worth 加 -less 构成，义为「无价值的；没用的」
由 worth 与 while 复合，义为「值得花时间的」
由 worthy 加 -ness 构成，义为「值得；可贵」

senses.title: Value in money
senses.definition: the amount of money that something would bring if sold
senses.definitionCN: 某物出售时能得到的钱数
senses.example: The old bicycle is not worth much, but I would not sell it for anything.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧自行车不值多少钱，但我多少钱也不卖。
senses.why: The core meaning is measured value: how much a thing is worth on a scale of money.
senses.whyCN: 核心意思是可衡量的价值：一件东西在钱的刻度上值多少。

senses.title: Deserving of something
senses.definition: having enough value or merit to justify the cost, effort or time
senses.definitionCN: 有价值到足以抵得上所付出的钱、力或时间
senses.example: This book is worth reading twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书值得读两遍。
senses.why: Once value is measured against effort, the word turns into a judgement: is the cost repaid?
senses.whyCN: 一旦把价值与付出相比，这个词就变成一种判断：所付是否值得。

senses.title: The quality that matters
senses.definition: the real importance or usefulness of a person or thing, apart from money
senses.definitionCN: 人或物在金钱之外的真实重要性或用处
senses.example: He proved his worth in the first month of the job.
senses.exampleCN: 他在工作的第一个月就证明了自己的价值。
senses.why: Once the scale is not money but usefulness, the same noun measures a person instead of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 当刻度不是钱而是用处时，同一个名词衡量的就从物变成了人。

senses.title: What one owns
senses.definition: the total of a person's money and property, as in net worth
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的钱财与产业总额，如 net worth
senses.example: The fire took everything of worth in the house.
senses.exampleCN: 那场火烧掉了屋里所有值钱的东西。
senses.why: The noun can also gather all the valuable things together, so it names a body of property.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也能把值钱的东西收拢在一起，于是指一整套财产。

intro.en: Worth is Old English weorth, meaning value or price, related to the verb weorthan, to become.
intro.cn: worth 来自古英语 weorth，意为价值或价格，与动词 weorthan（成为）相关。

items.en: weorth named the value of a thing, what it was reckoned at.
items.cn: weorth 指一物的价值，即它被估作多少。

items.en: Cousin words in German and Dutch still mean worth or value.
items.cn: 德语与荷兰语的同源词仍表示价值。

items.en: worth was used with a following noun of price, as worth ten pounds.
items.cn: worth 后面常接表示价钱的名词，如 worth ten pounds。

items.en: The adjective use without a verb grew fixed, as in worth a try.
items.cn: 不带系动词的形容词用法固定下来，如 worth a try。

items.en: The suffix -ship built worship from it, and -y built worthy.
items.cn: 后缀 -ship 由它造出 worship，-y 造出 worthy。

note.en: The first group holds the derivatives that grow from this root, the second holds other words for value.
note.cn: 第一组收由这个词根长出的派生词，第二组收其他表示价值的词。

entries.definition: Deserving respect or attention.
entries.definitionCN: 值得的；可敬的

entries.definition: Having no value at all.
entries.definitionCN: 无价值的

entries.definition: Worth the time spent on it.
entries.definitionCN: 值得花时间的

entries.definition: The amount of money a thing is worth.
entries.definitionCN: 价值；价钱

entries.definition: The money asked for a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 价格

entries.definition: The quality of deserving praise.
entries.definitionCN: 优点；功绩

normalIntro.en: Worth is an uninflected adjective and a noun at the same time, and the th is soft.
normalIntro.cn: worth 同时是不变化的形容词和名词，th 发清音。

normal.en: Worth is followed by a noun or an -ing word, never by to: worth reading, not worth to read.
normal.cn: worth 后接名词或 -ing 形式，不用 to：worth reading，而非 worth to read。

normal.en: The th is the unvoiced one, as in think, not the one in this.
normal.cn: 这里的 th 是清音，如 think，而不是 this 里的浊音。

normal.en: Worthless and worthy are opposites built with two different endings.
normal.cn: worthless 与 worthy 是用两种词尾造出的一对反义词。

normal.en: Worthwhile joins worth and while, since time is what is spent.
normal.cn: worthwhile 由 worth 与 while 复合，因为花掉的是时间。

normal.en: Worship was once worth-ship, which links honour with value.
normal.cn: worship 原是 worth-ship，把敬意与价值连在一起。

abstract.en: A pointer stopped at a mark nobody can quite read.
abstract.cn: 指针停在一个谁也读不准的刻度上。

abstract.en: A watch kept for its accuracy rather than its price.
abstract.cn: 一只留着是因为准，而不是因为值钱。

abstract.en: A month of work that answers a question about a person.
abstract.cn: 一个月的工作回答了一个关于人的问题。

examples.en: The tickets are worth every penny.
examples.cn: 这些票每一分钱都值。

examples.en: It is worth asking him before you decide.
examples.cn: 决定之前值得问问他。

examples.en: She proved her worth as a member of the team.
examples.cn: 她证明了自己作为队员的价值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我思」——值得的东西，值得「我思」上一整天。

root: 古英语 weorth（价值；价格），与 weorthan（成为）相关；-y 得 worthy，-less 得 worthless，-ship 得 worship。

sensesIntro.en: Measured value comes first, then the judgement that a cost is repaid, then the importance that money cannot measure, and finally the property one owns.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是可衡量的价值，再是「付出的值得」这一判断，接着是钱量不出的重要性，最后是拥有的财产。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pointer stopped at an unreadable mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：停在读不准的刻度上的指针。

branches.en: The price branch: a bicycle worth very little.
branches.cn: 价钱分支：不值多少钱的自行车。

branches.en: The judgement branch: a book worth reading twice.
branches.cn: 判断分支：值得读两遍的书。

branches.en: The person branch: proving worth in a first month.
branches.cn: 人分支：第一个月就证明价值。

branches.en: The property branch: everything of worth lost in a fire.
branches.cn: 财产分支：火中失去的所有值钱之物。

branches.en: The measure branch: one word for price and for human worth.
branches.cn: 衡量分支：一个词兼指价钱与人的价值。

intro.en: Worth is a bare stem, and three endings give it three very different children: worthy, worthless and worship.
intro.cn: worth 是裸词干，三个词尾生出三个很不一样的孩子：worthy、worthless 与 worship。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the Latin words below measure value and merit in another tradition.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语；下面的拉丁词在另一传统中衡量价值与功劳。

definition_zh: 教育的；与教育相关的；有教育意义的；用于教学的；教育机构的；受教育程度的；教育技术的；教育心理与教育不平等的
definition_en: relating to education or to teaching, or serving to instruct and improve knowledge
core_image: 一位老师在黑板上把一道线拉长，学生顺着这条线自己走到了没教过的地方
scene: 课堂上黑板已经写满，老师却仍在往边上添新的一行。 The teacher keeps writing past the filled board, and that habit makes every lesson deeply educational.
sceneCN: 这里 educational 是「有教育意义的、能教人的」（第 2 个义项：有教育意义的）；句意：老师把线延长到尚未讲过的地方，让学生顺着走进去，这是最有教育意义的做法。图中可辨识物件：黑板、延长的粉笔线、学生的手、未擦净的旧字、打开的课本。

pos.zh: 教育的；教育性的；有教育意义的

derivatives.zh: 教育；教育学
教育；培养
在教育上
教育学家；教育工作者
教育者

senses.title: Of education: belonging to the institution
senses.titleCN: 教育的：属于教育制度的
senses.definition: relating to the system, institutions, or process of education
senses.definitionCN: 与教育制度、机构或过程相关的
senses.example: The country spends a small share of its budget on educational infrastructure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家把预算中很小的一部分用于教育基础设施。
senses.why: Educational is education plus -al. Education comes from Latin educatio 'a rearing, training', from educare 'bring up'. The adjective simply marks what belongs to that process.
senses.whyCN: educational 是 education 加 -al。education 出自拉丁语 educatio“养育、培养”，源于 educare“抚养”。这个形容词只是标记“属于这一过程的东西”。

senses.title: Instructive: able to teach something
senses.titleCN: 有教育意义的：能教给人东西
senses.definition: providing knowledge or moral improvement, often outside a classroom
senses.definitionCN: 提供知识或道德提升，且常发生在课堂之外
senses.example: The failure was more educational than the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 这次失败比那堂课更有教育意义。
senses.why: Here -al shifts from 'belonging to education' to 'having the effect of teaching'. A museum, a mistake, or a game can be educational without being part of a school.
senses.whyCN: 这里 -al 从“属于教育”转为“具有教导效果”。博物馆、一次失误、一个游戏都可以是 educational，而不属于学校。

senses.title: For teaching: materials made to instruct
senses.titleCN: 用于教学：为教而造的材料
senses.definition: designed or used for teaching, as in educational books, games, or software
senses.definitionCN: 为教学而设计或使用的，如教育书籍、游戏或软件
senses.example: The app was marketed as educational but taught little.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用以教育为卖点，却几乎没教什么。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a market category: educational toys promise instruction as a product feature. The word now describes intent rather than result.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词成了市场类别：教育玩具把“教导”当作产品卖点。此时它描述“意图”，而非“结果”。

senses.title: Of attainment: how far schooling went
senses.titleCN: 受教育程度：上到哪一级
senses.definition: concerning the level of schooling a person or group has completed
senses.definitionCN: 关于个人或群体完成的教育层级
senses.example: Educational attainment predicts income more strongly than birthplace.
senses.exampleCN: 受教育程度对收入的预测力比出生地更强。
senses.why: Statistics turns a process into a level. 'Educational attainment' counts years and certificates, which is a measurable proxy for what the process gave.
senses.whyCN: 统计把过程变成一个层级。“受教育程度”计年数与证书，作为该过程所给之物的可测代理。

senses.title: Of technology: tools built for learning
senses.titleCN: 教育技术的：为学习而造的工具
senses.definition: relating to digital or mechanical tools used to support teaching and learning
senses.definitionCN: 与支持教与学的数字或机械工具相关的
senses.example: Educational technology promised personalisation and delivered screens.
senses.exampleCN: 教育技术承诺个性化，交付的却是屏幕。
senses.why: The compound 'educational technology' treats teaching as a field that can be engineered. The adjective keeps its institutional sense but attaches to machines.
senses.whyCN: 复合词 educational technology 把教学当作可被工程化的领域。形容词保持其制度义，却接到了机器上。

senses.title: Of psychology: learning as a subject of study
senses.titleCN: 教育心理的：把学习当作研究对象
senses.definition: concerning the psychological study of learning, motivation, and instruction
senses.definitionCN: 关于学习、动机与教学心理研究的
senses.example: Educational psychology studies how feedback changes retention.
senses.exampleCN: 教育心理学研究反馈如何改变记忆保持。
senses.why: A discipline name built on the adjective means 'the psychology of education'. The word marks the application of one field to the concerns of another.
senses.whyCN: 以这个形容词构成的学科名，意为“教育过程的心理学”。这个词标记一个领域对另一个领域的应用。

senses.title: Of inequality: gaps in what schooling delivers
senses.titleCN: 教育不平等的： schooling 所给之物的差距
senses.definition: concerning differences in access, resources, or outcomes among groups
senses.definitionCN: 关于不同群体在入学机会、资源或结果上的差异
senses.example: Educational inequality persists even when funding is equalised.
senses.exampleCN: 即使经费拉平，教育不平等依然存在。
senses.why: The adjective allows policy to name the arena of a gap without naming its cause. 'Educational inequality' locates the difference in outcomes, not in genes or income.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词让政策能说出差距所在的场域，而不必说出原因。“教育不平等”把差异定位在结果上，而不在基因或收入上。

senses.title: Of value: what a thing teaches
senses.titleCN: 教育价值：一物能教什么
senses.definition: the worth of an experience or object measured by what it teaches
senses.definitionCN: 按“能教什么”来衡量一段经历或一个物件的价值
senses.example: The documentary's educational value outweighed its inaccuracies.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片的教益超过了它的失实之处。
senses.why: Value language asks for a return: what did the learner get? Educational value is the pedagogy of an object, whether or not anyone planned it.
senses.whyCN: 价值语言要求回报：学习者得到了什么？教育价值就是一个物件的“教学性”，无论是否有人刻意设计。

intro.en: Educational is education plus -al. Education entered English in the 16th century from Latin educatio 'a rearing, training', from educare 'bring up, rear'. educare is related to educere 'lead out', and the old 'drawing out' idea is often mentioned, though the direct source is educare rather than educere.
intro.cn: educational 是 education 加 -al。education 于 16 世纪经拉丁语 educatio“养育、培养”进入英语，源于 educare“抚养、培育”。educare 与 educere“引出”相关，“把潜能引出来”的旧说常被提及，但直接来源是 educare，而非 educere。

items.en: Educational psychology, educational technology and educational inequality become established compound terms in research and policy.
items.cn: 教育心理学、教育技术、教育不平等成为研究与政策中的固定复合术语。

items.en: Educational is recorded as the adjective of education; the dating is approximate.
items.cn: educational 作为 education 的形容词见于记载；此处年代为大致估计。

items.en: Education is borrowed from Latin educatio, naming the rearing and training of a child.
items.cn: education 借自拉丁语 educatio，指对儿童的养育与培养。

items.en: educare 'bring up, rear' and educere 'lead out' are related but not identical: educare is frequentative in form, suggesting repeated care, while educere stresses leading forth.
items.cn: educare“抚养、培育”与 educere“引出”相关但不相同：educare 形式上有反复意味，暗示持续的照料；educere 则强调“引出”。

items.en: ducere 'to lead' comes from PIE *deuk- 'to lead'. The same root gives duct, conduct, introduce and produce, all involving leading or bringing.
items.cn: ducere“引导”出自原始印欧语 *deuk-“引导”（重构形式）。同一词根给出 duct、conduct、introduce、produce，都含“引、带”之意。

note.en: The first group separates true relatives from two genuine different-root neighbours; the second compares words that share only part of the meaning.
note.cn: 第一组把真正的同族词与两个不同词根的撞形词分开；第二组比较只共享部分含义的词。

entries.definition: a version of a published work. It comes from edere 'give out', from ex- plus dare 'give', not from educare 'rear'.
entries.definitionCN: 出版物的一种版本。它出自 edere“给出”，即 ex- 加 dare“给”，与 educare“养育”无关。

entries.definition: a large building. It comes from aedes 'building' plus facere 'make', with no connection to education.
entries.definitionCN: 大型建筑物。它出自 aedes“建筑”加 facere“制造”，与 education 无关。

entries.definition: the verb behind education, from educare. It is the source relation, not a look-alike.
entries.definitionCN: education 背后的动词，出自 educare。它是来源关系，不是撞形词。

entries.definition: giving useful information or a moral lesson. It is close to educational in sense 02, but stresses the lesson delivered.
entries.definitionCN: 提供有用信息或道德教训的。它与 educational 第 02 义接近，但强调所传递的教训。

entries.definition: relating to formal study at schools or universities. It is narrower than educational and often contrasts with practical.
entries.definitionCN: 与学校或大学的正式学习相关的。它比 educational 窄，且常与 practical 相对。

entries.definition: relating to teaching methods. It is more technical than educational and focuses on how, not what or where.
entries.definitionCN: 与教学方法相关的。它比 educational 更技术化，关注“怎么教”，而不是教什么、在哪里教。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real parts of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: educational is education plus -al, the same pattern as national and personal.
normal.cn: educational 是 education 加 -al，和 national、personal 一样。

normal.en: The root educare 'rear' is related to educere 'lead out': teaching as leading someone out of where they were.
normal.cn: 词根 educare“养育”与 educere“引出”相关：教学就是把一个人从原处引出来。

normal.en: ducere 'lead' also gives conduct, introduce and produce.
normal.cn: ducere“引导”还给出 conduct、introduce、produce。

normal.en: edition and edifice look like education but belong to dare 'give' and facere 'make'.
normal.cn: edition 与 edifice 看着像 education，却分属 dare“给”与 facere“造”。

normal.en: A museum can be educational without being educational in the institutional sense.
normal.cn: 一座博物馆可以是 educational（有教益），却不必是制度意义上的 educational。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a blackboard extended past the lesson, and a student walking along it.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上一条线被延长到课程之外，一名学生沿着它走。

abstract.en: The same line appears as a system, an attainment level, a toy, a technology, a psychology, an inequality, and a value.
abstract.cn: 同一条线可以显形为制度、受教育程度、玩具、技术、心理学、不平等与价值。

abstract.en: Every sense asks who is being led, and how far past the lesson they go.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都在问：被引领的是谁，又比课程多走了多远。

examples.en: The museum runs educational programmes for local schools.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆为当地学校开设教育项目。

examples.en: The game is educational without feeling like homework.
examples.cn: 这个游戏有教育意义，却不像作业。

examples.en: Educational attainment varies widely across the region.
examples.cn: 该地区的受教育程度差异很大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱就开心脑」——爱学习就开心动脑，越学越有教益 → educational 教育的、有教育意义的

root: 拉丁语 educatio“养育、培养”＝educare“抚养、培育”＋-atio（动作名词后缀）；educare 与 educere“引出”相关，后者＝ex-“出”＋ducere“引导”。educational＝education＋-al（形容词后缀）。核心是“把人从原处引出来”。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: a line drawn past the lesson. What changes is whether the line is an institution, an effect, a product, a level, a tool, a research field, a gap, or a value.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：一条画到课程之外的线。变化的只是这条线是制度、效果、产品、层级、工具、研究领域、差距，还是价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a teacher extends a chalk line past what has been taught, and students follow it.
core.cn: 核心意象：老师把粉笔线延长到已教内容之外，学生顺着走。

branches.en: INSTITUTION AND EFFECT: first the adjective marks what belongs to schooling, then what teaches outside it.
branches.cn: 制度与效果：形容词先标记属于学校教育的东西，再标记在校外教人的东西。

branches.en: MATERIALS: intent is built into toys and software, so the word describes design rather than result.
branches.cn: 材料：意图被做进玩具与软件，于是这个词描述设计而非结果。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: the process is converted into years and certificates, a level that can be compared.
branches.cn: 测量：过程被换算成年数与证书，成为可比较的层级。

branches.en: A FIELD OF STUDY: one discipline applies itself to education, producing educational psychology.
branches.cn: 研究领域：一门学科把自身应用于教育，产生教育心理学。

branches.en: VALUE AND GAP: the same line lets policy locate inequality and lets critics ask what an object teaches.
branches.cn: 价值与差距：同一条线让政策定位不平等，也让批评者追问一物教了什么。

intro.en: Educational is education plus -al. The suffix -al, from Latin -alis, forms relational adjectives; English first borrowed education, then added the adjective ending.
intro.cn: educational 是 education 加 -al。后缀 -al 出自拉丁语 -alis，构成关系形容词；英语先借入 education，再加形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The base verb is educare 'bring up, rear', related to educere 'lead out' (ex- 'out' plus ducere 'lead'). ducere supplies duct-, visible in conduct, introduce and produce.
latinIntro.cn: 词基动词是 educare“抚养、培育”，与 educere“引出”（ex-“出”＋ducere“引导”）相关。ducere 提供 duct- 词干，见于 conduct、introduce、produce。

items.meaning: relating to education, or serving to teach
items.meaningCN: 与教育相关的；有教益的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The trip had real educational value.
items.exampleCN: 这次旅行有真正的教益。

items.meaning: the process of rearing and teaching
items.meaningCN: 养育与教学的过程（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.exampleCN: 教育在学校之前很久就开始了。

items.example: They educated their children at home.

items.meaningCN: 教育者（-or 表示施动者）
items.exampleCN: 这位教育者设计了课程。

items.example: The two districts are educationally unequal.
items.exampleCN: 这两个学区在教育上并不平等。

items.meaning: one who studies or promotes education
items.meaningCN: 教育学家；教育改革推动者
items.example: The educationalist argued for smaller classes.
items.exampleCN: 这位教育学家主张缩小班级规模。

items.meaning: having the power to teach or improve
items.meaningCN: 有教育作用的；能起教化作用的
items.example: The experience was educative rather than pleasant.
items.exampleCN: 这段经历与其说愉快，不如说有教益。

items.meaningCN: 可教育的；有学习能力的
items.example: The test measured whether the child was educable.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试测量这个孩子是否具备受教育能力。

items.meaningCN: 男女同校的（co- 表示“共同”）
items.exampleCN: 这所学院于 1970 年改为男女同校。

items.example: Good questions educe what students already suspect.
items.exampleCN: 好问题能引出学生已有的猜想。

latinEntries.meaning: a rearing, training; the source of education
latinEntries.meaningCN: 养育、培养；education 所本的拉丁动作名词

definition_zh: 一排；一列；划船；连续的一段时间；（口语）争吵
definition_en: a line of things or people, to move a boat with oars, a period of continuous success, or a noisy quarrel
core_image: 一串首尾相连的东西：椅子排成行，船桨把水面划出一道直线
scene: 教室里椅子排得整整齐齐。 The students sat quietly in the first row of the classroom.
sceneCN: 这里 row 是「一排；一列」（第 1 个义项：横向排成的一行）；句意：学生们安静地坐在教室的第一排。

pos.zh: 一排；一列；划船；（口语）争吵

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 后缀构成，义为「划船者；划艇选手」
由现在分词转名词，义为「划船运动」

senses.title: A line of things
senses.definition: a straight line of people or things side by side
senses.definitionCN: 人或物肩并肩排成的一条直线
senses.example: There is a row of shops near my home.
senses.exampleCN: 我家附近有一排商店。
senses.why: Things placed one after another along a line form the basic picture.
senses.whyCN: 东西沿一条线首尾相接地摆放，构成了这个词最基本的画面。

senses.title: To move a boat with oars
senses.definition: to make a boat move forward using oars
senses.definitionCN: 用桨使船前进
senses.example: We rowed across the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 我们划船穿过湖面。
senses.why: Oars pull the water in long straight lines, like a row of strokes.
senses.whyCN: 船桨在水面拉出一道道长直线，与「一排」的线性意象相通，故借指划船。

senses.title: Continuous success
senses.definition: a period of repeated wins or events, used in phrases like in a row
senses.definitionCN: 接连发生的胜负或事件，用于 in a row 等短语
senses.example: Our team has won five games in a row.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队已经连赢五场。
senses.why: Successes lined up one after another are like objects placed in a row.
senses.whyCN: 接连的胜利像排成一行的物体，一个紧接一个，故由排列义引申出连续义。

senses.title: A noisy quarrel
senses.definition: a loud argument between people, informal British English
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间的大声争执，英式英语口语
senses.example: They had a row about the money.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为了钱吵了一架。
senses.why: This sense is generally considered a separate word of unknown origin that merged in sound with the line word.
senses.whyCN: 一般认为这是一个来源不确定的同音异源词，因读音相同而在书写上与「一排」混同。

intro.en: Row as a line comes from Old English rāw, while row as an argument is a separate word of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: row 的「一排」义源自古英语 rāw；「争吵」义则是一个来源不确定的同音异源词。

items.en: A Germanic root related to straight lines is reconstructed for the line sense.
items.cn: 「一排」义一般认为可重构出与「直线排列」相关的日耳曼语词根。

items.en: Rāw means a line or row of things.
items.cn: 古英语 rāw 意为一行、一列，指事物排成的直线。

items.en: Row keeps the line sense; the boat sense grows from pulling oars in lines.
items.cn: 中古英语 row 保留排列义；划船义由船桨成排划水的动作发展而来。

items.en: The quarrel sense first appears in the eighteenth century with no secure etymology.
items.cn: 「争吵」义首见于十八世纪，词源无定论，多认为是另一个词的同音混同。

items.en: In a row for continuous wins becomes a fixed phrase.
items.cn: 现代英语中 in a row 固定为表示「连续」的短语，广泛用于比分与纪录。

note.en: Row has a sound-alike verb and near-meaning words about lines and boats.
note.cn: row 有一个同音异源的近形词，近义词集中在排列与划船两个义场。

entries.definition: a cooked mixture of flour and fat for sauces
entries.definitionCN: （烹饪用的）油面酱，拼写相近但词源是法语，与 row 无关，只是形近

entries.definition: not cooked
entries.definitionCN: 生的；未煮过的，字母顺序颠倒后读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to make a loud deep sound
entries.definitionCN: 吼叫；轰鸣，与 row 拼写只差一个字母，但属拟声词，来源不同

entries.definition: a row of people or things
entries.definitionCN: 排；行列，泛指一切排成的直线，与 row 的排列义基本重合

entries.definition: to move a small boat with a paddle
entries.definitionCN: 用短桨划（小艇），动作相近但用具与船型不同

entries.definition: an angry argument
entries.definitionCN: 争吵，正式的说法，对应 row 的口语争吵义

normalIntro.en: Five ways to remember row through lines, oars and rows of seats.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕排列、船桨与成排座位的记忆路径。

normal.en: ROW looks like a straight line of letters, R-O-W, one after another.
normal.cn: ROW 三个字母排成一条直线，就像一排东西首尾相连。

normal.en: ROW a boat: the oar pulls the water in one long line each stroke.
normal.cn: 划船时每桨在水面拉出一道长直线，和「一排」意象相通。

normal.en: Cinema seats come in rows: front row means the closest seats.
normal.cn: 影院座位成排：front row 就是离银幕最近的前排。

normal.en: Five wins IN A ROW: think of five gold medals lined up in a row.
normal.cn: 五连胜 in a row：想象五块金牌排成一行的画面。

normal.en: ROW with two readings: /rəʊ/ for lines and boats, /raʊ/ for fights.
normal.cn: row 两种读法：/rəʊ/ 指排与划船，/raʊ/ 指吵架，靠重音区分。

abstract.en: See chairs stretch to the horizon, all standing in one endless row.
abstract.cn: 想象椅子一直排到天边，构成一条望不到头的长排。

abstract.en: Feel the oar slice the water, leaving a straight line behind the boat.
abstract.cn: 感受船桨切开水面，在船尾留下一道笔直的水线。

abstract.en: Picture medals pinned side by side, each win another item in the row.
abstract.cn: 想象奖牌一枚枚并排钉在墙上，每一枚都是这排里的一个新成员。

examples.en: The teacher asked us to stand in a row.
examples.cn: 老师让我们站成一排。

examples.en: They rowed the little boat to the other side of the river.
examples.cn: 他们把小船划到了河对岸。

examples.en: She has been late for school three days in a row.
examples.cn: 她已经连续三天上学迟到了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肉」——一排烤肉架上一排肉，排排都是肉；row 读音近似「肉」

root: 「一排」义源自古英语 rāw（行列），属日耳曼语源；「争吵」义一般认为来源不确定，是十八世纪出现的同音异源词，两者书写混同但并非同根。

sensesIntro.en: Row moves from a straight line of things to pulling oars, to continuous wins, and to an informal quarrel.
sensesIntro.cn: row 从成排的直线出发，延伸到划船动作、连续纪录，再到口语中的争吵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: things placed one after another in a line
core.cn: 核心意象：东西一个接一个排成的直线

branches.en: The line image covers both static rows and repeated wins.
branches.cn: 直线意象同时覆盖静止的成排与接连的胜负。

branches.en: Each oar stroke draws a line through the water.
branches.cn: 每一桨都在水面划出一道线，划船由此挂靠排列义。

branches.en: Rowing a boat and rowing crops of seats share the ordered-line feeling.
branches.cn: 划船与成排座位共享「有序直线」的语感。

branches.en: The quarrel sense is a sound-alike word, not grown from the line image.
branches.cn: 争吵义是同音异源词，并非从排列意象长出。

branches.en: Rows give order to seats, houses and shops along a street.
branches.cn: 成排给座椅、房屋与街边商店带来秩序感。

intro.en: Row builds few derivatives; most compounds keep the line or boat sense.
intro.cn: row 的派生词不多，合成词大多保留排列或划船义。

latinIntro.en: Row is Germanic in origin with no Latin relatives, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: row 属日耳曼语源词，没有拉丁同族词，故不列拉丁词条。

items.example: Each rower pulls hard on the oar.

items.meaning: the sport of racing boats with oars
items.example: Rowing is popular at the university.
items.exampleCN: 划船运动在这所大学很流行。

items.meaning: a small boat moved with oars
items.example: They rented a rowboat for the afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 他们下午租了一条划艇。

items.example: He was absent twice in a row.

items.meaning: the line of seats closest to the front
items.example: The kids fought for the front row.

items.meaning: a house built in a continuous row with shared side walls
items.example: They live in a red brick row house.
items.exampleCN: 他们住在一栋红砖排屋里。

items.meaning: to make a loud fuss or quarrel
items.example: The fans kicked up a row at the referee.
items.exampleCN: 球迷们对裁判大吵大闹。

items.meaning: the part of a prison for prisoners waiting execution
items.meaningCN: 死囚区；等待处决的囚犯牢房区
items.example: The novel is set on death row.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说以死囚区为背景。

definition_zh: 代替；反而；却
definition_en: in the place of something else; as a replacement or an unexpected opposite
core_image: 两扇门之间你推开了旁边那一扇
scene: 本想看电影，结果去了公园。 It rained, so we watched a film at home instead.
sceneCN: 这里 instead 是「反而」（第 2 个义项：出现相反结果）；句意：下雨了，我们只好在家看电影。

derivatives.zh: 古旧名词，义为「位置；用处」（in one's stead）
instead 加介词构成的短语介词，义为「而不是」

senses.title: In place of something
senses.definition: in the place of someone or something else
senses.definitionCN: 处在别的人或事物的位置上
senses.example: There was no tea, so we drank coffee instead.
senses.exampleCN: 没有茶，我们改喝咖啡。
senses.why: The next door opens when one is locked.
senses.whyCN: 一扇门锁上，旁边那扇便被推开。

senses.title: An unexpected opposite result
senses.definition: introducing what happened instead of what was expected
senses.definitionCN: 引出与预期相反的结果
senses.example: He did not help; instead, he laughed.
senses.exampleCN: 他没帮忙，反而大笑。
senses.why: The wrong door swings open with a grin.
senses.whyCN: 被推开的竟是那扇带着讥笑的门。

senses.title: Instead of: phrase use
senses.definition: used before a noun or verb-ing to replace it
senses.definitionCN: 后接名词或动名词，表示替换
senses.example: Walk instead of taking the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 走路别坐车。
senses.why: Two doors hang side by side; you choose one.
senses.whyCN: 两扇门并排，只推其一。

intro.en: Instead is in + stead, from Old English stede, a place. To take something in stead is to take it in its place.
intro.cn: instead 由 in + stead 构成，stead 出自古英语 stede「地方」；in stead 即「处其位」。

items.en: Old English stede meant a place or spot; place names still keep it.
items.cn: 古英语 stede 意为地方；地名中仍有留存。

items.en: The phrase in stedes meant in the place of.
items.cn: 短语 in stedes 意为居于其位。

items.en: Middle English in stead solidified into one written word.
items.cn: 中古英语 in stead 固化为一个词。

items.en: instead of grew into the standard replacement phrase.
items.cn: instead of 发展成标准的替换短语。

items.en: The old noun survives only in the legal in one's stead.
items.cn: 古名词只存活在法律用语 in one's stead 中。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the stead family. The meaning group compares words of replacement and contrast.
note.cn: 形近组收录 stead 词族；词义组比较替换与转折类词。

entries.definition: the old noun for place.
entries.definitionCN: 古名词，指位置。

entries.definition: firmly standing in its place.
entries.definitionCN: 站稳其位的，即稳定的。

entries.definition: the compound preposition.
entries.definitionCN: 短语介词。

entries.definition: more willingly; on the contrary.
entries.definitionCN: 宁愿；相反。

entries.definition: replacing something.
entries.definitionCN: 代替。

entries.definition: as another choice.
entries.definitionCN: 作为另一种选择。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the place root, the two-doors image and the instead-of rule.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用「地方」词根、双门意象与 instead of 规则。

normal.en: in plus stead (place): taken into another's place.
normal.cn: in 加 stead（位置）：顶了别人的位。

normal.en: stead survives in legal in one's stead.
normal.cn: stead 只在法律用语 in one's stead 里存活。

normal.en: instead of plus noun or verb-ing.
normal.cn: instead of 后接名词或动名词。

normal.en: steady shares the place root: steady in its place.
normal.cn: steady 同根：稳在其位。

normal.en: He laughed instead: the unexpected door.
normal.cn: 他反而大笑：推开了那扇意外的门。

abstract.en: One image: two doors, one hand, the second chosen.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：两扇门，一次选择，推开了第二扇。

abstract.en: Instead is the plan B hiding beside plan A.
abstract.cn: instead 是躲在计划 A 旁边的计划 B。

abstract.en: Where one chair is empty, another slides in.
abstract.cn: 一把椅子空了，另一把滑过来。

examples.en: Use honey instead of sugar.
examples.cn: 用蜂蜜代替糖。

examples.en: She did not cry; instead, she smiled.
examples.cn: 她没哭，反而笑了。

examples.en: If Tuesday is full, come Wednesday instead.
examples.cn: 周二满了就改周三来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因斯特德」：因原计划黄了，换了斯特德来顶替， instead。

root: 古英语 stede「地方」→ 短语 in stedes「处其位」→ 中古英语 in stead → 现代英语 instead；同根词 stead、steady、steadfast。

sensesIntro.en: Instead is the second door: a seat taken in another's place, the grin of an opposite result, and the phrase that picks between two doors.
sensesIntro.cn: instead 是第二扇门：顶替他人的位置、相反结果的讥笑，以及在两扇门之间替你作选择的短语。

core.en: A hand that pushes the neighboring door when the first is shut.
core.cn: 第一扇门关上时，推开了旁边那扇门的手。

branches.en: SUBSTITUTION: drank coffee instead.
branches.cn: 替换：改喝咖啡。

branches.en: CONTRAST: instead, he laughed.
branches.cn: 转折：他反而大笑。

branches.en: CHOICE: walk instead of taking the bus.
branches.cn: 选择：走路别坐车。

branches.en: PREFERENCE: picking the second door.
branches.cn: 偏好：推开第二扇门。

branches.en: SURPRISE: what happened was the opposite.
branches.cn: 意外：结果恰恰相反。

intro.en: Instead keeps the old stead alive and pairs with instead of.
intro.cn: instead 保留了古词 stead，并与 instead of 搭配。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entries: this compound is pure English.
latinIntro.cn: 无拉丁条目：该复合词是纯正英语造词。

items.example: He came in his father's stead.

definition_zh: 第二；其次；其二
definition_en: used to introduce the second point in a list or argument
core_image: 发言清单上的第二格：第一点讲完，手指移到下一个格子里
scene: 老师让大家说出两个减少塑料垃圾的办法。 First, we should bring our own bags. Secondly, we can refuse plastic straws.
sceneCN: 这里 secondly 是「第二；其次」（第 1 个义项：用来引出列举或论证中的第二点），承接前面的 first，把话题推进到第二条建议。

pos.zh: 第二；其次；用于引出列举中的第二点

collocations.zh: 第一、第二、最后（列举框架）
其次，也是更重要的一点
第一和第二（口语中不规范，常被纠正）

基础词名词用法，义为「秒；片刻」

second 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「（人员的）临时借调」

senses.title: To introduce the second point in a list
senses.definition: used to introduce the second item, reason, or argument after «first» or «firstly»
senses.definitionCN: 在 first 或 firstly 之后，用来引出第二项、第二条理由或第二个论点
senses.example: First, the plan is cheap. Secondly, it is easy to carry out.
senses.exampleCN: 第一，这个方案很省钱。其次，它很容易实施。
senses.why: The ordinal number second names what comes after the first, and the adverb ending -ly turns it into a signpost word that guides listeners through a list.
senses.whyCN: 序数词 second 表示「排在第一之后的那个」，加上副词后缀 -ly 后变成路标词，专门在列举时为听众指引第二个要点。

senses.title: To add a second, supporting argument
senses.titleCN: 追加第二条支持性论据
senses.definition: used in formal writing or debate to add a further reason that strengthens the case already made
senses.definitionCN: 用于正式写作或辩论中，补充一条强化前文立场的进一步理由
senses.example: The rule is unfair; secondly, it would be almost impossible to enforce.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规定不公平；其次，它几乎无法执行。
senses.why: Once a list frame is established, the speaker naturally reuses the same signpost pattern to stack reasons, so secondly grows from naming a position into carrying a new supporting argument.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「列条目」的框架建立起来，说话者就自然复用同一路标模式来叠加理由，secondly 便从「标记位置」长出「承载新论据」的功能。

intro.en: Secondly is a modern signpost adverb built from the ordinal number second plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: secondly 是现代英语里的列举路标副词，由序数词 second 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: The root is Latin secundus, meaning «following, next in order», from the verb sequi, «to follow».
items.cn: 词根是拉丁语 secundus，意为「跟随其后的、依次的下一个」，来自动词 sequi「跟随」。

items.en: Latin secundus passed into Old French as second, keeping the meaning of «next after the first».
items.cn: 拉丁语 secundus 进入古法语变成 second，仍表示「紧跟第一之后的」。

items.en: Middle English borrowed second from Old French around the thirteenth century as an ordinal adjective.
items.cn: 中古英语约在十三世纪从古法语借入 second，作序数形容词使用。

items.en: In Modern English, second combined with the productive adverb suffix -ly to form secondly, first recorded as a discourse marker in formal argument.
items.cn: 现代英语中，second 与能产性副词后缀 -ly 结合形成 secondly，最早记录为正式论证中的话语标记。

items.en: Today secondly normally appears only in enumerated speech or writing, paired with firstly or first, and is not used for the physical sense of «the second time».
items.cn: 如今 secondly 一般只出现在列条目的口语或书面语中，与 firstly 或 first 配对使用，不用于表示「第二次」这类实际次数含义。

note.en: Secondly is easy to confuse with its cousin words built on the same ordinal root.
note.cn: secondly 容易与同根的序数词族词混淆，下面两组帮你分清。

entries.definition: the ordinal number or adjective; also a unit of time
entries.definitionCN: 序数词「第二」或时间单位「秒」，是 secondly 的基础词

entries.definition: less important; relating to the second stage
entries.definitionCN: 次要的；中等的；由 second 派生的形容词

entries.definition: previously owned; not from the original source
entries.definitionCN: 二手的；间接得来的；由 second 与 hand 合成

entries.definition: introduces the first point in a list
entries.definitionCN: 引出列举中的第一点，常与 secondly 前后呼应

entries.definition: in addition; used to add another stronger point
entries.definitionCN: 此外；而且；正式语体中追加更强的论点

entries.definition: coming immediately after in order or sequence
entries.definitionCN: 接下来；随后；比 secondly 更口语化的过渡词

normalIntro.en: Five grounded ways to remember secondly.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于构词和搭配的记忆法。

normal.en: second + -ly: the ordinal number second «next after first» plus the common adverb suffix -ly, exactly like «firstly».
normal.cn: second（第二）加副词后缀 -ly，构造与 firstly（第一）完全平行。

normal.en: Latin sequi «to follow»: secondly marks the point that follows the first one.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 sequi「跟随」：secondly 标记的就是「跟在第一点后面」的那一点。

normal.en: Pair memory: whenever you hear firstly, expect secondly to arrive next.
normal.cn: 配对记忆：听到 firstly，下一个多半就是 secondly。

normal.en: Speech skeleton: firstly… secondly… finally… is the classic three-point speech frame.
normal.cn: 演讲骨架：firstly… secondly… finally… 是经典的三点式发言框架。

normal.en: Essay signpost: in argumentative writing, secondly opens the second body paragraph.
normal.cn: 写作路标：议论文里 secondly 常开启第二个主体段落。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder: you have stepped on rung one (firstly) and now lift your foot to rung two — secondly.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子：已踩上第一级（firstly），正抬脚踏上第二级——secondly。

abstract.en: Two checkboxes on a to-do list: the first is ticked, your pen hovers over the second — that hover is secondly.
abstract.cn: 待办清单上两个方框：第一个已打勾，笔尖悬在第二个上方——这一悬停就是 secondly。

abstract.en: A train leaving station one and pulling into station two: each stop of the argument is a numbered platform.
abstract.cn: 列车驶离一站、进站二：论证的每一站都是编了号的月台，secondly 就是第二月台到站声。

examples.en: Firstly, the room is too small; secondly, the rent is too high.
examples.cn: 第一，房间太小；其次，租金太高。

examples.en: Secondly, we must think about how the new rule affects younger students.
examples.cn: 其次，我们必须考虑新规定对低年级学生的影响。

examples.en: She listed two reasons: secondly, the bus would be faster than walking.
examples.cn: 她列了两条理由：其次，坐公交比走路快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞看得了」——第一点已经看完了，塞进脑子里看第二点，看得了第二点就轮到 secondly。

root: 拉丁语 secundus（依次的、跟随其后的）← 动词 sequi（跟随）；经古法语 second 进入中古英语；现代英语加副词后缀 -ly 构成列举路标词。

sensesIntro.en: Two discourse senses: a list signpost, and a carrier for the second supporting argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个话语义项：既是列举路标，也是第二条支持性论据的载体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stepping to the second mark on an ordered list
core.cn: 核心意象：在有序清单上迈向第二个标记点

branches.en: ENUMERATION: secondly names the second point after first or firstly.
branches.cn: 列举线：secondly 在 first 或 firstly 之后点名第二个要点。

branches.en: ARGUMENT: the second point is stacked to reinforce the case already opened.
branches.cn: 论证线：第二个要点用来强化已经展开的立场。

branches.en: SEQUENCE: it inherits the Latin idea of following what came before.
branches.cn: 顺序线：它继承了拉丁语「跟随在前者之后」的观念。

branches.en: SIGNPOST: the -ly form works like firstly and finally to structure speech.
branches.cn: 路标线：-ly 形式与 firstly、finally 一样为发言搭建结构。

branches.en: FORMALITY: it marks formal, planned discourse rather than casual chat.
branches.cn: 语域线：它标记正式、有准备的语篇，而非随意闲谈。

intro.en: Secondly is a transparent formation: ordinal stem + adverb suffix.
intro.cn: secondly 构词透明：序数词干加副词后缀，一目了然。

latinIntro.en: The ordinal stem traces back to Latin secundus «following».
latinIntro.cn: 序数词干可追溯到拉丁语 secundus「跟随其后的」。

items.exampleCN: 第一是成本，其次是安全。

definition_zh: 有罪的；内疚的；感到愧疚的
definition_en: responsible for breaking a law or doing something wrong; feeling shame about it
core_image: 低着头的孩子，双手绞在身后，明知自己做错了事
scene: 打碎了花瓶的孩子站在客厅角落，头埋得很低不敢看妈妈。 The boy felt guilty about breaking his mother's favorite vase.
sceneCN: 这里 guilty 是「内疚的、愧疚的」（第 2 个义项：心里感到有错）；句意是男孩打碎妈妈心爱的花瓶后深感内疚。

derivatives.zh: 由 guilty 去掉 -y 构成，义为「罪行；内疚」
由 guilty 加 -ly 构成，义为「内疚地；心虚地」

senses.title: Responsible for a crime
senses.definition: shown by law to have done something illegal
senses.definitionCN: 经法律认定做了违法之事
senses.example: The court found him guilty of theft.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭判定他犯有盗窃罪。
senses.why: The head-bowed picture first belongs to the courtroom, where guilt is proven.
senses.whyCN: 低头认错的画面首先出现在法庭，那里有罪与否由证据裁定。

senses.title: Feeling shame inside
senses.definition: feeling unhappy because you have done something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 因做错事而心里难受
senses.example: She felt guilty about lying to her friend.
senses.exampleCN: 她因对朋友撒谎而内疚。
senses.why: Not all wrongs reach a court; the same bowed head appears inside the heart.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有错事都会上法庭，同样低垂的头也会出现在心里。

senses.title: Looking or sounding ashamed
senses.definition: showing guilt through face, voice, or behavior
senses.definitionCN: 通过表情、声音或行为流露愧疚
senses.example: He gave a guilty smile when the teacher asked.
senses.exampleCN: 老师一问，他露出了心虚的笑。
senses.why: Inner shame leaks outward; the feeling paints itself on the face.
senses.whyCN: 内心的愧疚会外泄，情绪自己画在脸上。

senses.title: Deserving blame for a small fault
senses.definition: responsible for a mistake or carelessness, not a crime
senses.definitionCN: 对错误或疏忽负有责任（非罪行）
senses.example: Who is guilty of leaving the window open?
senses.exampleCN: 是谁没关窗户？
senses.why: Blame scales down; the courtroom word shrinks to fit everyday faults.
senses.whyCN: 责备可大可小，法庭用语缩小后用来指日常过失。

senses.title: Enjoyed with mild shame
senses.definition: used to describe a pleasure one feels slightly bad about
senses.definitionCN: 形容明知不太好却仍然享受的事物
senses.example: Chocolate cake is my guilty pleasure.
senses.exampleCN: 巧克力蛋糕是我的罪恶快感。
senses.why: Enjoyment and shame can share one bite; the odd pair creates a fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 享乐与愧疚可以咬在同一口里，奇特的组合固定成短语。

intro.en: Guilty grows from an old English word about debt and wrong payment.
intro.cn: guilty 源自一个关于「欠债、亏欠」的古英语词。

items.en: Old English gylt meant fault, sin, or even a payment due for a wrong.
items.cn: 古英语 gylt 意为过错、罪，甚至指因过错而应付的款项。

items.en: The adjective gyltig meant guilty or owing, joining the noun with -ig.
items.cn: 加 -ig 构成形容词 gyltig，意为有罪的、亏欠的。

items.en: Middle English guilty kept both the legal and the moral meanings.
items.cn: 中古英语 guilty 保留法律义与道德义。

items.en: Modern English fixed the court phrase plead guilty and the feeling phrase feel guilty.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了 plead guilty（认罪）与 feel guilty（感到内疚）。

items.en: The playful phrase guilty pleasure appeared in recent centuries.
items.cn: guilty pleasure（罪恶快感）这一俏皮说法是近几个世纪出现的。

note.en: Words near guilty in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 guilty 形近或义近的词。

entries.definitionCN: 行会；与 guilty 词形相近，词源无关

entries.definition: the fact or feeling of having done wrong

entries.definition: covered with a thin layer of gold

entries.definition: feeling shame about something done
entries.definitionCN: 羞愧的，强调丢脸感

entries.definition: deserving blame
entries.definitionCN: 该受责备的

entries.definition: not guilty of a crime or fault
entries.definitionCN: 无罪的；清白的，guilty 的反义

normalIntro.en: Five memory hooks for guilty.
normalIntro.cn: 五条 guilty 的记忆钩子。

normal.en: guilt + y: the y paints the feeling on the face
normal.cn: guilt + y：词尾 y 把内疚画在脸上。

normal.en: plead guilty is the fixed courtroom phrase
normal.cn: plead guilty（认罪）是法庭固定用语。

normal.en: feel guilty about + the wrong thing
normal.cn: feel guilty about + 错事，是最常用搭配。

normal.en: guilt and gilt sound the same but shine differently
normal.cn: guilt（内疚）与 gilt（镀金）同音不同义。

normal.en: guilty pleasure is a phrase worth memorizing whole
normal.cn: guilty pleasure 值得整条背下来。

abstract.en: a child hiding a broken vase behind his back
abstract.cn: 孩子把打碎的花瓶藏到身后。

abstract.en: eyes sliding sideways during a question
abstract.cn: 被提问时眼珠偷偷往旁边溜。

abstract.en: a courtroom hammer paused mid-air
abstract.cn: 法槌悬在半空，等待判决。

examples.en: The jury declared the man not guilty.
examples.cn: 陪审团宣布该男子无罪。

examples.en: I always feel guilty when I skip my homework.
examples.cn: 一不写作业我就感到内疚。

examples.en: Her guilty expression gave the secret away.
examples.cn: 她心虚的表情泄露了秘密。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「给提」——做错事的人低着头等着被「给提」起来批评，guilty 就是心虚。

root: 源自古英语 gylt（过错、罪、应付的款项），加形容词后缀 -ig 构成 gyltig；词义从「亏欠」延伸到「有罪」，核心画面是「欠下一笔还不清的错」。

sensesIntro.en: From court conviction the word moves inward to shame, outward to looks, sideways to small faults, and playfully to pleasures.
sensesIntro.cn: 从法庭定罪走向内心羞愧，外显为神情，缩小到日常过失，最后俏皮地用于享乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowed head and hands behind the back
core.cn: 核心意象：低垂的头与背在身后的手

branches.en: the court says yes
branches.cn: 法庭认定有罪

branches.en: the heart says sorry
branches.cn: 心里说对不起

branches.en: the face shows it
branches.cn: 表情藏不住

branches.en: small faults shared out
branches.cn: 日常过失的归属

branches.en: joy with a wink of shame
branches.cn: 带着一丝愧疚的快乐

intro.cn: guilty 只用极简词尾，下面展示这些词尾的用法与近邻词。

latinIntro.cn: 与 guilt 词族搭配的拉丁语系词。

items.example: A guilty look spread over her face.
items.exampleCN: 她脸上泛起心虚的神色。

items.example: Nothing feels guiltier than a lost promise.
items.exampleCN: 没有什么比失约更让人愧疚。

items.example: The guiltiest moment came at midnight.

items.example: The judge set the innocent free.

definition_zh: 展示；陈列；显示；表露；显示屏
definition_en: to put something where it can be seen, or to show a quality, feeling, or image
core_image: 一面折叠的旗子被完全展开
scene: 博物馆的玻璃展柜里灯光正好，讲解员把青铜器摆到最显眼的位置。 The museum will display the bronze vessel in a glass case.
sceneCN: 这里 display 是「陈列、展示」（第 1 个义项：把某物放在可见处）；句意：博物馆将把青铜器陈列在玻璃展柜中。

derivatives.zh: display 加表示者的后缀构成，义为「展示者」
display 加 able 构成，义为「可展示的」

senses.title: Put something where it can be seen
senses.definition: to arrange an object so that people can look at it
senses.definitionCN: 摆放物品让人们观看
senses.example: The shop displays its new coats in the window.
senses.exampleCN: 商店把新外套陈列在橱窗里。
senses.why: The first image is a banner unfurled: Old French desploiir meant unfold and spread out, so display is a folded thing opened to view.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初的意象是展开的旗帜。古法语 desploiir 意为「展开、铺开」，所以 display 就是折叠之物被打开给人看。

senses.title: Show a quality or feeling
senses.definition: to let a quality, emotion, or attitude be seen
senses.definitionCN: 让某种品质、情绪或态度被看见
senses.example: He displayed no fear during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨中他没有表现出恐惧。
senses.why: An inner state is treated like a flag: when it becomes visible to others, it is displayed.
senses.whyCN: 内在状态被当作一面旗：当它对别人可见时，就被展示了出来。

senses.title: Show information on a screen
senses.definition: to present data or images on an electronic screen
senses.definitionCN: 在电子屏幕上呈现数据或图像
senses.example: The screen displays the bus number.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕显示公交车的线路号。
senses.why: The modern screen sense keeps the original idea of spreading something before the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 现代屏幕义保留了最初「铺开在眼前」的想法。

senses.title: An exhibition or a show
senses.definition: an arrangement of objects or effects for people to see
senses.definitionCN: 为观看者布置的物品或效果
senses.example: We watched a fireworks display on the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在河边看了一场烟花表演。
senses.why: The noun names the whole arranged spectacle rather than one object.
senses.whyCN: 名词指整个被布置出来的景观，而不是单件物品。

intro.en: Display began with cloth: a folded flag or sail spread open, and the literal unfolding became the model for showing things.
intro.cn: display 从布开始：折叠的旗或帆被展开，字面的展开成为展示万物的模型。

items.en: Latin displicare meant to scatter, to unfold, from dis- apart and plicare to fold.
items.cn: 拉丁语 displicare 意为「散开、展开」，由 dis-（分开）加 plicare（折叠）构成。

items.en: Old French desploiir meant to unfold or spread out a banner or sail.
items.cn: 古法语 desploiir 意为展开旗帜或船帆。

items.en: Around the fourteenth century English took display in the sense of unfurling a flag.
items.cn: 约十四世纪英语借入 display，意为展开旗帜。

items.en: The sense widened from flags to objects, feelings, and spectacles.
items.cn: 词义从旗帜扩大到物品、情绪与景观。

items.en: The word now covers shop windows, screens, and electronic monitors.
items.cn: 如今这个词覆盖橱窗、屏幕与电子显示器。

note.en: These words stand near display in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 display 相邻。

normalIntro.cn: 用「展开旗帜」的画面和 display 词族来记。

normal.cn: on display 表示某物被摆出来供人参观。

senses.title: Cannot happen or be done

intro.en: Impossible joins the Latin negating prefix in-, here im-, with possibilis, able to be done, from posse, to be able. It entered English through Old French in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: impossible 由拉丁语否定前缀 in-（此处作 im-）加 possibilis「可做到的」（词基 posse「能够」）构成，十四世纪经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Latin posse meant to be able; the participle possibilis meant capable of happening.
items.cn: 拉丁语 posse 意为能够；分词 possibilis 指可能发生的。

items.en: The negative prefix in- turned it into impossibilis, not able to be.
items.cn: 否定前缀 in- 将其变为 impossibilis「不可能的」。

items.en: Old French impossible carried the word into medieval Europe.
items.cn: 古法语 impossible 把该词带入中世纪欧洲。

items.en: Middle English impossible first described things that could not happen.
items.cn: 中古英语 impossible 先指不可能发生之事。

items.en: Modern English extended it to unbearable people and situations, and coined impossibility and impossibly.
items.cn: 现代英语扩展到难忍的人与处境，并造出 impossibility 与 impossibly。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the possible family and a sound-alike word. The meaning group compares impossibility words.
note.cn: 形近组收录 possible 词族与一个近音词；词义组比较表示不可能的词。

entries.definition: a thing that may happen; the opposite direction of the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 可能性。同一标尺的反方向。

entries.definitionCN: 不可通行的。发音相近，但词基是 pass。

entries.definition: in an impossible manner or degree.
entries.definitionCN: 不可能地；难以置信地。

entries.definition: not practical to do, though perhaps possible.
entries.definitionCN: 不可行的。或许可能但不实际。

entries.definition: not allowed or worth discussing at all.
entries.definitionCN: 不予考虑。根本不值得讨论。

entries.definition: too shocking or unlikely to be considered.
entries.definitionCN: 难以想象的。令人震惊而不敢考虑。

normal.cn: im 加 possible：加上 im- 前缀，可能就转身离开。

normal.en: nothing is impossible is the favorite motivational phrase.
normal.cn: nothing is impossible 是最流行的励志语。

normal.en: next to impossible keeps a hair of hope: almost, but not quite.
normal.cn: next to impossible 还留有一丝希望：几乎，但不是绝对。

normal.en: an impossible guest is a locked door at dinner.
normal.cn: an impossible guest 是餐桌上一扇打不开的门。

normal.en: Do not mix impossible and impassable: one is doing, one is passing.
normal.cn: 别混淆 impossible 与 impassable：一个关于做，一个关于通行。

abstract.en: One image: a door with no handle on your side.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一扇在你这一侧没有把手的门。

abstract.en: Impossible is a verdict, not a mood: it says the world says no.
abstract.cn: impossible 是判定而非情绪：它说世界说了不。

abstract.en: Use it in three grades: unlikely, impossible, unbearable.
abstract.cn: 分三档使用：不太可能、不可能、难以忍受。

examples.cn: 十个人塞进这辆车是不可能的。

examples.en: Without a map, finding the cabin was next to impossible.
examples.cn: 没有地图，找到小屋几乎不可能。

examples.en: The manager faced an impossible choice between staff and budget.
examples.cn: 经理面临人员与预算之间无解的抉择。

sensesIntro.en: Impossible closes doors: of events, of patience, of temper and of truth.

branches.en: TEMPER: an impossible person.

branches.en: TRUTH: claims that cannot both be true.

branches.en: SCALE: from next to impossible to nothing is impossible.

definition_en: a large keyboard instrument whose strings are struck by hammers; also the skill of playing it and its part in a piece of music
core_image: 一排黑白琴键在灯下向远处延伸，琴盖被支起
scene: 琴房的门关着，木地板被午后的光照得发亮，一个孩子把手指悬在黑白琴键上方不敢落下。 The piano stood open in the corner, waiting for the first note.
sceneCN: 这里 piano 指「钢琴」（第 1 个义项：那台键盘乐器）；句意为钢琴开着盖立在角落，等着第一个音。图中可辨识物件：黑白琴键、支起的琴盖、谱架。

pos.zh: 钢琴；钢琴演奏；钢琴声部

derivatives.zh: 由 piano 加 -ist 构成，义为「钢琴家」
由意大利语 piano（弱）与 forte（强）复合而成，是钢琴的旧称

senses.title: The keyboard instrument
senses.definition: a large musical instrument with a row of black and white keys that send hammers to strike strings inside a wooden case
senses.definitionCN: 一种大型乐器，黑白琴键带动木箱内的琴槌敲击琴弦发声
senses.example: The piano stood open in the corner of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴开着盖立在房间角落。
senses.why: Italian piano meant soft, and the instrument's full name pianoforte said it could sound both soft and strong, which was exactly what the older harpsichord could not do.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 piano 意为轻柔，这件乐器的全名 pianoforte 是在说它既能弱也能强，而这正是旧式羽管键琴做不到的事。

senses.title: The skill or subject of playing it
senses.definition: the art or school subject of playing this instrument, as in studying piano at a conservatory
senses.definitionCN: 演奏这件乐器的技艺或学校科目，如音乐学院里的钢琴专业
senses.example: He studied piano for ten years before he ever performed in public.
senses.exampleCN: 他学了十年钢琴才第一次公开演出。
senses.why: English lets the name of an instrument stand for the skill practised on it, so piano becomes a subject you can study, teach, or take an exam in.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许乐器名直接指在这件乐器上练出来的技艺，于是 piano 成了一门可以学、可以教、可以考试的科目。

senses.title: The piano part in a score or ensemble
senses.definition: the line or part written for the piano in a score, especially when it plays alongside other instruments
senses.definitionCN: 总谱中写给钢琴的那一行或那一声部，尤指与其他乐器合奏时
senses.example: The piano enters softly under the strings in the second movement.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章里，钢琴在弦乐之下轻轻进入。
senses.why: Once a score lists instruments by name, each named staff can be called by its instrument, so the piano printed on the page becomes the piano heard in the hall.
senses.whyCN: 总谱一旦按乐器名称分列各行，每一行就能直接用乐器名来称呼，于是印在纸上的「钢琴」变成了大厅里听到的钢琴声部。

intro.en: Piano is a shortened Italian phrase: the full name of the instrument described its ability to sound soft as well as loud.
intro.cn: piano 是意大利语短语的缩略：这件乐器的全名描述的是它既能弱也能强。

items.en: Planus meant flat, level, or plain, and it is the distant source of the Italian word for soft and smooth.
items.cn: planus 意为平的、平坦的、平实的，是意大利语中表示柔和、平滑那个词的远源。

items.en: Italian piano meant soft or smooth, and musicians used it as a direction to play quietly.
items.cn: 意大利语 piano 意为轻柔、平滑，乐师用它作「轻声演奏」的指示。

items.en: Pianoforte joined piano, soft, with forte, strong, to name a harpsichord-like instrument that could do both.
items.cn: pianoforte 把表示「弱」的 piano 与表示「强」的 forte 拼在一起，用来命名一种既能弱又能强、类似羽管键琴的乐器。

items.en: English borrowed the instrument and shortened the long name to piano, which then became the everyday word.
items.cn: 英语借来这件乐器，并把长名缩短为 piano，随后它成了日常说法。

items.en: Modern English uses piano for the instrument, for the skill, and for the part, while the full name survives mostly in formal writing.
items.cn: 现代英语用 piano 指乐器、技艺与声部，而旧的全名大多只留在正式文字里。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Italian word and the forms built on it; the near-meaning group gathers other keyboard instruments.
note.cn: 形近组沿着这个意大利语词及其派生形式排列；近义组收其他键盘乐器。

entries.definition: The full eighteenth-century name of the instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 这件乐器在十八世纪的全名。

entries.definition: A musical direction meaning very soft.
entries.definitionCN: 音乐术语：极弱地。

entries.definition: The art or technique of piano playing.
entries.definitionCN: 钢琴演奏的艺术或技巧。

entries.definition: A large keyboard instrument that makes sound by driving air through pipes.
entries.definitionCN: 靠气流通过音管发声的大型键盘乐器；管风琴。

entries.definition: An older keyboard instrument whose strings are plucked rather than struck.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的键盘乐器，琴弦被拨动而非被敲击；羽管键琴。

entries.definition: A row of keys on an instrument, or an electronic instrument built around such keys.
entries.definitionCN: 乐器上的一排琴键，或围绕琴键制成的电子乐器。

normalIntro.en: The word began life as an Italian direction for soft playing, and the instrument took that word as its name.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词原本是意大利语里「轻声演奏」的指示，乐器后来把这个词当成了自己的名字。

normal.en: Piano in Italian means soft, so the marking piano on a score still tells a player to play quietly.
normal.cn: 意大利语 piano 意为轻柔，所以谱面上的 piano 记号至今仍在告诉演奏者放轻。

normal.en: The full name pianoforte joined soft and strong, because this instrument could change volume in a way the harpsichord could not.
normal.cn: 全名 pianoforte 把「弱」与「强」拼在一起，因为这件乐器能改变音量，而羽管键琴不能。

normal.en: English cut the long name down to piano, and the short form is now the ordinary word in every shop that sells one.
normal.cn: 英语把长名砍成 piano，这个短形式如今成了每家琴行里的日常说法。

normal.en: Pianist adds -ist to piano, and the stress moves to the first syllable even though the spelling keeps the o.
normal.cn: pianist 在 piano 后加 -ist，重音移到第一个音节，但拼写里仍留着那个 o。

normal.en: The plural is pianos, not pianoes, because the word came from Italian and simply takes an s.
normal.cn: 复数是 pianos 而不是 pianoes，因为这个词来自意大利语，直接加 s。

abstract.en: A word meaning soft became the name of an instrument that can be very loud, because its novelty was the power to be quiet.
abstract.cn: 一个意为「轻柔」的词，成了一台能很响的乐器的名字，因为它的新鲜处正在于能安静下来。

abstract.en: Eighty-eight keys, one short word: the name grew shorter as the instrument grew common.
abstract.cn: 八十八个琴键，一个短词：乐器越普及，名字就越短。

abstract.en: The same word names the object, the skill and the line in the score, since all three begin at one keyboard.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指那件东西，也指那门技艺和谱面上的那一行，因为三者都从同一排琴键开始。

examples.en: The piano stood open in the corner of the room.
examples.cn: 钢琴开着盖立在房间角落。

examples.en: She has her piano lesson every Thursday afternoon.
examples.cn: 她每周四下午上钢琴课。

examples.en: The piano enters softly under the strings.
examples.cn: 钢琴在弦乐之下轻轻进入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮阿诺」——琴键一按，声音轻得像耳语，piano 本来正是「轻柔」的意思。

root: 意大利语 piano（轻柔、平滑）源自拉丁语 planus（平的、平实的）；pianoforte 由 piano 与 forte（强）合成，英语缩略为 piano。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the instrument that can be soft and strong; from the object come the skill practised on it and the part it plays in a score.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是那件能弱能强的键盘乐器；由这件实物分出在它上面练成的技艺，以及它在总谱里担任的声部。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: black and white keys running away under a lamp, the lid propped open.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯下一排黑白琴键向远处延伸，琴盖被支起。

branches.en: a wooden case with its lid propped open
branches.cn: 琴盖支起的木制琴箱

branches.en: a child's hand hovering above the keys before the first lesson
branches.cn: 第一堂课之前悬在琴键上方的小手

branches.en: a practice room heard through a closed door
branches.cn: 隔着关着的门听见的练琴声

branches.en: a page where the piano line waits under the violins
branches.cn: 谱面上等在提琴声部下方的钢琴行

branches.en: a trio playing with one player at the keyboard
branches.cn: 三人合奏，其中一人在键盘前

intro.en: A Latin adjective for flat lies behind the Italian word for soft, and the instrument's double name was later cut in half.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「平」的形容词是意大利语「轻柔」一词的来源，而乐器的双名后来被砍掉了一半。

latinIntro.en: Italian piano goes back to Latin planus, flat or plain, so the Latin entry belongs to the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 意大利语 piano 可追到拉丁语 planus（平的、平实的），所以这条拉丁词与它同属一族。

items.meaningCN: 意大利语最高级词尾：极

definition_zh: 危险的；有危害的
definition_en: likely to cause harm or injury
core_image: 写着警示语的黄色三角牌
scene: 春游前，班主任反复叮嘱不要靠近湖边那片湿滑的斜坡。 The teacher said the wet slope near the lake is very dangerous.
sceneCN: 这里 dangerous 是「危险的」（第 1 个义项：很可能造成伤害）；句意是老师说湖边湿滑的斜坡非常危险。

derivatives.zh: dangerous 的基础词，义为「危险」
由 en- 加 danger 构成，义为「危及」
由 dangerous 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「危险地」

senses.title: Likely to cause physical harm
senses.definition: able to hurt people or damage bodies and things
senses.definitionCN: 可能伤人或损坏身体的
senses.example: Swimming in this river alone is dangerous, so we always go together.
senses.exampleCN: 独自在这条河里游泳很危险，所以我们总是结伴去。
senses.why: When danger becomes a quality of the thing itself, the adjective fixes it there.
senses.whyCN: 当「危险」成为事物本身的属性，形容词便把它固定在那事物上。

senses.title: Risky in a wider sense
senses.definition: harmful to health, plans or results, not only to the body
senses.definitionCN: 对健康、计划或结果有害，不只针对身体
senses.example: Staying up too late every night is dangerous for your grades.
senses.exampleCN: 每晚熬夜太晚会危害你的成绩。
senses.why: What hurts the body hurts projects too, so the word stretched to outcomes.
senses.whyCN: 伤身体的也能毁计划，于是词义延伸到了结果层面。

intro.en: Dangerous simply attaches the adjective ending to danger.
intro.cn: dangerous 只是把形容词词尾接到 danger 上。

items.en: dominium meant lordly power, from dominus, lord.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dominium 意为领主的支配权，来自 dominus（主人）。

items.en: dangier kept the sense of power to harm.
items.cn: 古法语 dangier 保留「伤害之威权」的意思。

items.en: English danger first meant such power over people.
items.cn: 英语 danger 最初指对人的支配权。

items.en: Adding -ous formed dangerous, describing things full of that harming power.
items.cn: 加 -ous 构成 dangerous，形容充满伤害之力的东西。

items.en: Now dangerous describes snakes, storms, habits and ideas alike.
items.cn: 如今 dangerous 既形容蛇、风暴，也形容习惯和思想。

note.en: These words describe harm, or come from the same danger family.
note.cn: 这些词描述危害，或来自 danger 词族。

entries.definition: the noun behind this adjective
entries.definitionCN: 危险（名词基础词）

entries.definition: to put someone in danger
entries.definitionCN: 危及

entries.definition: in a dangerous way
entries.definitionCN: 危险地

entries.definition: shocking and extreme; ends the same way, unrelated
entries.definitionCN: 骇人的（词尾相同，词源无关）

entries.definition: full of risk
entries.definitionCN: 有风险的

entries.definition: involving hazard, often formal
entries.definitionCN: 有危害的（较正式）

entries.definition: not safe
entries.definitionCN: 不安全的

entries.definition: able to cause death
entries.definitionCN: 致命的

entries.definition: free from harm
entries.definitionCN: 安全的

normalIntro.en: Stack the word: danger plus ous.
normalIntro.cn: 把词叠起来记：danger 加 ous。

normal.en: danger + ous = dangerous, full of danger.
normal.cn: danger + ous ＝ dangerous，充满危险的。

normal.en: Comparing needs more and most: more dangerous, most dangerous.
normal.cn: 比较级要用 more/most：more dangerous、most dangerous。

normal.en: en- + danger = endanger: bad habits endanger your eyes.
normal.cn: en- + danger ＝ endanger：坏习惯会伤眼睛。

normal.en: Say the safety rhyme: safe is safe, dangerous is not.
normal.cn: 念安全口诀：safe 是安全，dangerous 是危险。

normal.en: Warning signs, wet floors and thin ice are all described as dangerous.
normal.cn: 警示牌、湿地、薄冰都用 dangerous 形容。

abstract.en: Picture the yellow triangle with a black lightning sign.
abstract.cn: 想象带黑色闪电符号的黄色三角牌。

abstract.en: Hear the teacher repeat the word twice before the trip.
abstract.cn: 听老师春游前把这个词重复两遍。

abstract.en: Feel your shoulders tighten when the bike wobbles near a truck.
abstract.cn: 体会自行车在卡车旁摇晃时肩膀绷紧的感觉。

examples.en: It is dangerous to run down the stairs with wet shoes.
examples.cn: 穿着湿鞋跑下楼梯很危险。

examples.en: Crocodiles are among the most dangerous animals in the river.
examples.cn: 鳄鱼是这条河里最危险的动物之一。

examples.en: The sign says the cliff path is closed and dangerous.
examples.cn: 牌子上写着悬崖小路已封闭且危险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「单脚儿斯」——只用「单脚儿」站在悬崖边斯哈斯哈喘气，太危险了

root: 由 danger（源自拉丁语 dominium「支配权」，经古法语 dangier「伤害之威权」）加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，字面为「充满危险的」。

sensesIntro.en: One ending turns a noun of harm into a quality of things.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个词尾把伤害的名词变成事物的属性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a yellow warning triangle
core.cn: 核心意象：写着警示语的黄色三角牌

branches.en: Hurting bodies: ice, snakes, stairs
branches.cn: 伤身的：冰面、蛇、楼梯

branches.en: Hurting plans and health
branches.cn: 损害计划与健康

branches.en: Anything likely to cause harm
branches.cn: 一切可能造成危害的

branches.en: Describing roads and animals
branches.cn: 形容道路与动物

branches.en: The opposite: safe and safe
branches.cn: 相对面：safe（安全的）

intro.en: The suffix -ous does all the work here.
intro.cn: 这里的构词全靠后缀 -ous。

latinIntro.en: The root domin- means lord; -ous comes from Latin -osus, full of.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 domin- 意为主人；-ous 来自拉丁语 -osus，意为充满。

items.exampleCN: smoking endangers health（吸烟危害健康）

definition_zh: 典型的；有代表性的；特有的
definition_en: showing the usual features of a group, or happening in the usual way
core_image: 一排相似的老房子，其中一栋可以代表整条街
scene: 海边小镇的早晨，渔船一条条回港，街上飘着鱼汤的味道。 A typical morning here begins with the boats coming in.
sceneCN: 这里 typical 是「典型的；有代表性的」（第 1 个义项：体现某一类事物共性特征）；句意为这里典型的早晨从渔船回港开始。可以代表整条街的那栋老房子，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 typical 加 -ly 构成，义为「典型地；通常」
由 typical 加 -ity 构成，义为「典型性」
由 typical 加前缀 a- 构成，义为「非典型的」

senses.title: The one that stands for all
senses.definition: having the features that most members of a group share
senses.definitionCN: 具有某一群体多数成员共有的特征
senses.example: A typical morning here begins with the boats coming in.
senses.exampleCN: 这里典型的早晨从渔船回港开始。
senses.why: The word points at a sample good enough to stand for the whole group.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指向一个足以代表整群的样本。

senses.title: The habit that marks you
senses.definition: showing the special character of a person or thing, often in a slightly critical way
senses.definitionCN: 显示某人某物特有的性格，常略带批评意味
senses.example: It was typical of him to arrive without calling.
senses.exampleCN: 不打电话就来，正是他一贯的作风。
senses.why: If a feature is shared by a group, it can also be the mark by which one member is known.
senses.whyCN: 若某特征是群体共有，也可成为辨认某个成员的特有标记。

intro.en: Typical is built on type plus the adjective ending -ical, and means of the stamp or the class.
intro.cn: typical 由 type 加形容词词尾 -ical 构成，意为「具有这一印模的」。

items.en: Typos named a blow and the mark left by it.
items.cn: typos 指一击以及它留下的印。

items.en: Typicus appeared in late Latin for something figurative.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 typicus 指具有图像或象征意味的东西。

items.en: The ending -ical joined type to make typical in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪 -ical 与 type 结合成 typical。

items.en: Science used it for a specimen that represents a whole species.
items.cn: 科学用它指代表整个物种的标本。

items.en: Everyday speech widened it to anything usual or characteristic.
items.cn: 日常语言把它扩展到一切寻常或有代表性的事物。

note.en: The first group shares the type stem, the second holds words of the same meaning.
note.cn: 第一组共享 type 词干，第二组是同义词。

entries.definition: In the usual manner.
entries.definitionCN: 通常；典型地

entries.definition: Not usual for its group.
entries.definitionCN: 非典型的

entries.definition: About current affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 时事的

entries.definition: Standing for a larger group.
entries.definitionCN: 有代表性的

entries.definition: Typical of a person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 特有的

entries.definition: Happening most often.
entries.definitionCN: 寻常的

normalIntro.en: Typical means of the type: the sample that wears the class face.
normalIntro.cn: typical 意为「属于这一类的」：长着这一类的脸的样本。

normal.en: Type plus -ical makes the adjective typical.
normal.cn: type 加 -ical 成形容词 typical。

normal.en: Typical of is the set phrase for a characteristic mark.
normal.cn: typical of 是表示「某物特有的」固定搭配。

normal.en: The a- in atypical means not.
normal.cn: atypical 里的 a- 表示「不」。

normal.en: Typically works as a sentence adverb: typically, it rained.
normal.cn: typically 常作句副词：typically, it rained。

normal.en: A typical example is chosen to speak for many.
normal.cn: 典型例子是被选来代表许多个的。

abstract.en: One plain house standing in a row of similar houses.
abstract.cn: 一排相似房屋中一栋普通的房子。

abstract.en: A sample jar labelled to represent a species.
abstract.cn: 标着物种名的标本瓶。

abstract.en: Rain arriving at the same hour every afternoon.
abstract.cn: 每天下午同一时刻到来的雨。

examples.en: This is a typical example of village architecture.
examples.cn: 这是乡村建筑的典型例子。

examples.en: It is typical of her to help without being asked.
examples.cn: 不用人求就帮忙，正是她的作风。

examples.en: Winter here is typical of the whole coast.
examples.cn: 这里的冬天代表了整个海岸一带。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提皮扣」——提起皮包就能当代表的那一位，最典型。

root: 由 type（类型、印模，源自希腊语 typos 一击与印痕）加形容词词尾 -ical 构成，本义为具有该类特征的，同族词有 typically、typicality、atypical。

sensesIntro.en: First the sample that stands for its class, then the trait that marks an individual.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是能代表类别的样本，再是标记个体的特性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one plain house that speaks for the row.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间足以代表整排的普通房子。

branches.en: The sample branch: one stands for many.
branches.cn: 样本分支：一个代表许多。

branches.en: The mark branch: the trait that names you.
branches.cn: 标记分支：能叫出你名字的特征。

branches.en: The ordinary branch: nothing unusual happens.
branches.cn: 寻常分支：没有特别的事发生。

branches.en: The judgement branch: typical can gently blame.
branches.cn: 评价分支：常带一点温和的抱怨。

branches.en: The science branch: a specimen defined by its type.
branches.cn: 科学分支：以模式标本定的物种。

intro.en: Typical is type plus -ical, and the family grows with -ly, -ity and the negative a-.
intro.cn: typical 是 type 加 -ical，词族靠 -ly、-ity 与否定前缀 a- 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The late Latin adjective typicus stands behind the English form, listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 英语形式背后是晚期拉丁语形容词 typicus，列在下面。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 typical 与 topical。
